records.title: Academic Program & Schedule
facts: Brentwood is a university preparatory school emphasizing academic excellence and authentic learning.
The Tripartite Program schedules academics Monday-Saturday mornings, with afternoons for arts/athletics, followed by supervised evening study ("Prep").
The oceanfront campus supports experiential learning, including marine biology and cultural trips.

records.title: Admissions Process
facts: Students attend Brentwood College School by their own choice.
The Admissions Team works to understand a student's reasons for wanting to join the school.

records.title: Admissions Process
facts: Brentwood College seeks students who value opportunities, embrace challenges, and can cultivate the boarding school community.
Admission is based on an applicant's academic potential, expressed desire to attend, and willingness to participate in extracurricular activities.
Prospective families can speak with the Admissions Team in person or online, and presentations are offered through online open houses or during travel.
An online inquiry form is available to start the application process.

records.title: Admissions Team
facts: The Admissions Team includes Director of Admissions Clayton Johnston, Associate Directors Andrea Torres Lopez and James Boswell, and Admissions Assistant Lorraine Walsh.
Clayton Johnston has served in various roles at Brentwood since 1994, including Houseparent and Director of Boarding.
Andrea Torres Lopez has experience in student recruitment across Canada and Latin America, and speaks English and Spanish.
James Boswell has expertise in secondary and post-secondary recruitment, coordinated International Programs at the University of Toronto, and is fluent in French and Spanish.
Lorraine Walsh has a background in preschool education and as an Elementary School Teacher's Assistant.

records.title: Application Payment Methods
facts: Application fees can be paid by bank draft or personal cheque to 'Brentwood College School' (US funds converted).
Credit card payments via Plastiq or Credit Card Authorization Form to accounts@brentwood.ca.
Canadian bank holders can use online banking (payee 'Brentwood College School') or Pre-Authorized Debit (PAD Form + voided cheque).
International payments via Flywire offer bank transfer/credit card in home currency with tracking.

records.title: Application Process
facts: Applications are for the upcoming school year, with a three-stage online process.
An account can be saved before submission, which includes parent/guardian and student sections.
Email confirmation is sent upon submission.

records.title: Financial assistance and fees
facts: Financial assistance applications use Apple Financial Services’ FACS process; Brentwood makes the award decision.
Returning families must reapply for financial aid annually.
The public page mixes 2027/28 fee wording with 2026 payment dates. Confirm the applicable year and amounts with Admissions using this source.

records.title: Grade 8 Admissions
facts: For more information about the Grade 8 Program, contact the Admissions Team.
Spaces for the coming school year are always limited.

records.title: New Families Information
facts: Brentwood College School welcomes newly admitted families.
The school provides support for questions related to starting at the school.
Resources are available for financial information, course selection, the first week of school, calendar of events, school documents, and travel information.

records.title: New Student Onboarding Process
facts: Parents/guardians sign a letter of intent and validate profile data in MySchool after student acceptance.
The Enrolment Agreement must be accepted in MySchool, and the deposit is due within 30 days of acceptance.
A student account with a Brentwood email is created upon deposit receipt, with login instructions sent to students and parents.
Students, with parents, select courses for academics, athletics, and arts.
Mid-year enrolments may consult Mr. Rick Rodrigues, Director of University Counselling, for course selection.

records.title: Returning Student Annual Tasks
facts: Parents/guardians must re-review the annually updated Student Handbook and Fees, then accept the Enrolment Agreement in MySchool.
The Accounting Team sends an email regarding the Enrolment Deposit.
Students, with parents, select courses over the winter midterm break.
Required forms include Informed Consent, Health (via BlueHealth), and a Food Services Questionnaire; Private Music Lessons are optional.

records.title: Supporting Documents for Application
facts: Submit documents individually as PDFs with English translations to admissions@brentwood.ca.

Required: one academic recommendation (English/Math teacher), one personal recommendation (non-family), previous/current school reports, passport-style photo, photocopy of birth certificate and passport.
A non-refundable $300 application fee is required.

records.title: Tour, Test, and Interview
facts: Campus tours by appointment Mon-Sat from 10:00 am; contact admissions@brentwood.ca or (250) 743-5521.
A 30-minute aptitude test is required (on-campus or proctored off-campus); SSAT results also accepted.
A 20-30 minute personal interview with an Admissions Director is required, on campus or via Zoom.

records.title: Boarding Houses

Houseparents and Assistant Houseparents live in adjoining suites within each house.

Over 80% of students board full-time. Grade 12 students can be Prefects to mentor younger students.

records.title: 20th Century World History 12
facts: 20th Century World History 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course explores themes of nationalism, imperialism, technological developments, and conflict in the 20th century.
Students participate in forum discussions, analyze political cartoons and documents, and deliver oral presentations.
Essential components include reading, speaking in class, and advocating a political perspective.

records.title: 3D Art & Sculpture
facts: The 3D Art & Sculpture course introduces students to design and sculptural techniques using materials like clay, wood, plastics, and soapstone.
In the fall term, the focus is on design and fabrication using machine shop and hand tools for projects like clock design or architectural structures.
The winter term covers clay modeling, hand-building forms, and creating abstract or freestanding sculptures, including human and animal forms.
The spring term introduces soapstone carving, one-piece mould-making, and casting techniques for jewelry and small carvings.
More advanced students can create their own design briefs and projects.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Studio Arts 3D 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: 3D Art & Sculpture Program
facts: The 3D Art & Sculpture program is diverse and expressive.
Students work with materials such as cardboard, wood, cement, and clay.
Instructors teach the design process, and students explore new topics each term, including traditional and abstract concepts.
The studio offers oceanfront views for inspiration and is equipped with tools and space for multi-media sculpture.
Finished student projects are showcased around campus, with public exhibits in the main entrance gallery of the Centre for Arts and Humanities.
Leyla Haslebacher is an instructor for this program.

records.title: 3D Pottery
facts: This course teaches wheel-thrown pottery for beginners or students with some experience.
Students will explore the ceramic medium creatively and artistically.
Technical processes learned include building pots by hand, surface decoration, glazing, and firing.
Ministry credit is awarded for Studio Arts 3D 10, 11, or 12.

records.title: AP Biology 11
facts: AP Biology 11 is an elective Advanced Placement science course for Grade 11 students.
The course covers key topics explaining the structure, function, and continuity of life.
Students explore biomolecules, cell structures and functions, evolution, natural selection, DNA, the cell cycle, and heredity.
The course also introduces biotechnology and its applications.
This course is the first half of a first-year university-equivalent course, involving notes, readings, labs, activities, and projects.
Upon completion, students receive Life Sciences 11 Ministry Credit.

records.title: AP Biology 12
facts: AP Biology 12 is an elective Advanced Placement science course for Grade 12 students.
The course focuses on core principles of living systems, including evolution, energy use, and information processing.
Students examine how interactions within and between biological systems create complex properties.
The course emphasizes hands-on activities like experiments, projects, and fieldwork to develop science skills.
Students will write the AP Biology exam in May.
AP Biology 11 is a prerequisite for this course.
AP Biology 11 and 12 cover overlapping material and incorporate Anatomy & Physiology 12 topics.
Upon completion, students receive AP Biology 12 and Anatomy and Physiology 12 Ministry Credits.

records.title: AP Calculus AB 12
facts: AP Calculus AB 12 is a Grade 12 Advanced Placement elective course in Mathematics.
The course focuses on fundamental calculus concepts, real-world applications, and logical arguments.
Topics include limits, continuity, differentiation and its applications, integration, differential equations, and applications of integration.
Students explore concepts through graphical, numerical, analytical, and verbal perspectives.
The course is equivalent to a first-semester college calculus course.
Students will write the AP Calculus AB exam in May.
A prerequisite for this course is the completion of Pre-Calculus 12 (recommended) or concurrent enrollment.

records.title: AP Chemistry 11
facts: AP Chemistry 11 is an elective Advanced Placement course for Grade 11 students.
The course covers key topics including biomolecules, cell structures and functions, evolution, natural selection, DNA, the cell cycle, heredity, and biotechnology.
It extends beyond regular Chemistry 11 topics and requires independent study due to its fast pace.
Successful completion awards Ministry Credit for Chemistry 11.
A strong recommendation for this course is proficiency in Science 10 and Math 10.

records.title: AP Chemistry 12
facts: AP Chemistry 12 is an elective Grade 12 science course.
The course covers units from Chemistry 12, with added topics in Thermodynamics and Applications of Thermodynamics.
It is a faster-paced course with increased complexity in some units compared to regular Chemistry 12.
Students will engage in problem-solving, multiple-choice calculations, and guided inquiry investigations.
Strong algebra skills are essential for this course.
Students will write the AP Chemistry exam in May.
The prerequisite for AP Chemistry 12 is AP Chemistry 11, with proficiency highly recommended.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Chemistry 12.

records.title: AP Chinese Language & Culture 12
facts: AP Chinese Language & Culture 12 is a Grade 12 Advanced Placement elective course in Languages.
The course emphasizes communication skills (interpersonal, interpretive, presentational) in real-life situations.
It develops proficiency in listening, speaking, reading, and writing Mandarin.
The curriculum fosters cultural understanding through Chinese traditions, practices, and contemporary society.
The course is taught almost exclusively in Mandarin.
Students will write the AP Chinese Language and Culture exam in May.
The prerequisite is Mandarin 12; students without this credit must interview with Ms. Yang for consideration.

records.title: AP Comparative Government & Politics 12
facts: AP Comparative Government & Politics 12 is an Advanced Placement elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students in Social Studies.
The course examines political systems through the lens of six countries: the United Kingdom, Nigeria, China, Russia, Iran, and Mexico.
It explores questions of power, governance, democracy, and political structures.
The course aims to develop informed global citizens with a critical perspective on political issues.
Much of the course involves discussion-based activities like seminars, current events discussions, presentations, and guest speakers.
Students will write the AP Comparative Government and Politics exam in May.
A profound interest in politics and governance is the most important quality for students.

records.title: AP Computer Science A 12
facts: AP Computer Science A 12 is an Advanced Placement elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students in Math.
The course provides an in-depth study of the Java computer language.
Students learn object-oriented programming basics and build a foundation for post-secondary disciplines.
Units of study include control structures, classes and objects, interfaces, arrays, inheritance, streams, recursion, and sorting methods.
The course develops practical coding and problem-solving skills.
Students will write the AP Computer Science A exam in May.
Prior coding experience is highly recommended for this course.

records.title: AP Computer Science Principles 12
facts: AP Computer Science Principles 12 is an entry-level elective course for Grade 11 and 12 students.
The course introduces foundations of modern computing, covering programming, algorithms, the Internet, big data, digital privacy and security, and societal impacts of computing.
Major units include digital information, the internet, introduction to algorithms and programming, big data: research and privacy, building apps, and creating and exploring tasks.
Students are assumed to have knowledge of introductory algebra.
Students complete two in-class performance tasks and write the AP Computer Science Principles exam in May.
Upon completion, students are awarded Ministry Credit for AP Computer Science Principles 12.

records.title: AP English 11
facts: AP English 11 is an Advanced Placement academic course for Grade 11 students.
Students cover the entire English 11 curriculum and also write timed, in-class synthesis, analysis, and argument papers.
Students receive credit for both English 11 and AP English Language and Composition 12.
This accelerated course is recommended for students who demonstrated consistent proficiency in English 10 competencies.
It requires more reading and critical writing than English 11, often involving unfamiliar texts under timed conditions.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Literary Studies 11 and AP English Language and Composition 12.

records.title: AP English Literature and Composition 12
facts: AP English Literature and Composition 12 is a dual credit course for Grade 12 students, combining advanced literary analysis with English Studies 12 skills.
The university-level course focuses on reading, analyzing, and writing about imaginative literature from various periods, including fiction, poetry, and drama.
Students engage in close reading and critical analysis to understand how writers use language, considering structure, style, themes, figurative language, imagery, and symbolism.
Writing assignments include expository, analytical, and argumentative essays that require analysis and interpretation of literary works.
The course is recommended for students who have consistently demonstrated proficiency or extending in prior English courses.
Students will write the AP English Literature & Composition exam in May.
Upon completion, students are awarded Ministry Credit for English Studies 12 and AP English Literature and Composition 12.

records.title: AP Environmental Science 12
facts: AP Environmental Science 12 is an elective course for Grade 12 students focusing on fundamental ideas shaping ecological and environmental systems.
The course examines energy transfer, Earth's interconnected systems, natural and biogeochemical processes, and their ability to recover from disturbances.
It explores interactions among species and environments, with attention to human alterations of natural systems over time.
Emphasis is placed on sustainability and developing practices that support the long-term survival of human societies and natural systems.
Students develop critical and scientific thinking skills and explore a wide range of interconnected topics.
Students will write the AP Environmental Science exam in May.
Upon completion, students are awarded Ministry Credit for AP Environmental Science 12.

records.title: AP French Language 12
facts: AP French Language 12 is an elective course for Grade 12 students.
The course emphasizes communication by applying interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational skills in real-life situations.
Students develop language skills and learn about various topics related to Francophone culture.
Learning activities include listening and reading comprehension, writing and oral communication tasks, and novel studies.
Students analyze authentic audiovisual resources to strengthen their understanding of real-world language use.
Students will write the AP French Language and Culture exam in May.
This course is recommended for students who have completed Immersion French or new students with significant immersion or Francophone background.

records.title: AP Macroeconomics 12
facts: AP Macroeconomics 12 is a college-level elective course for Grade 11 and 12 students, introducing principles applicable to an economic system as a whole.

The course emphasizes national income and price-level determination, and familiarizes students with economic performance measures, the financial sector, stabilization policies, economic growth, and international economics.
Students learn to use graphs, charts, and data to analyze, describe, and explain economic concepts.
Topics explored include GDP, inflation, interest rates, unemployment rates, fiscal and monetary policies, foreign exchange, and bonds, and their impact on everyday life.
Students will write the AP Macroeconomics exam in May.
Upon completion, students are awarded Ministry Credit for AP Macroeconomics 12.

records.title: AP Microeconomics 12
facts: AP Microeconomics 12 is a college-level elective course available to Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course introduces principles of economics related to individual economic decision-makers and the operation of product and factor markets.
Topics include income distribution, market failure, and the government's role in promoting efficiency and equity.
Students learn to use graphs, charts, and data for economic analysis.
Students will take the AP Microeconomics exam in May.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Microeconomics 12.

records.title: AP Music Theory 12
facts: AP Music Theory 12 is an Advanced Placement elective course.
It is designed for serious musicians wishing to further their knowledge or continue music studies post-Brentwood.
The course covers requirements for the AP Music Theory Exam held in May.
Topics include music fundamentals, melodic and harmonic dictation, contextual listening, sight singing, and stylistic composition.
Other areas covered are figured bass, melodic harmonization, and visual analysis techniques.
Prerequisites include some background in music studies up to an intermediate level, or at least 3 years of instrumental or vocal study.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Music Theory 12 (APMU 12).

records.title: AP Physics 11
facts: AP Physics 11 is an elective course for Grade 11 students that explores physics concepts with greater depth and mathematical rigor than Physics 11.
Students study kinematics, dynamics (one-dimensional, two-dimensional, circular, and rotational motion), statics, and fluid mechanics.
The course also covers work and energy, as well as momentum and impulse.
This is a fast-paced, rigorous course involving continuous problem-solving and experimental design, stretching mathematical skills.
Graphical analysis is a critical component of the work in this course.
Students will write the AP Physics 1 exam in May.
Pre-Calculus 11 completed (recommended) or concurrent enrollment is required as a prerequisite.

records.title: AP Physics 12
facts: AP Physics 12 is a Grade 12 Advanced Placement elective course in Science.
The course builds on AP Physics 11, focusing on forces, fields, energy conservation, and systems of particles.
Topics include thermodynamics, electrostatics, circuits, electromagnetism, waves, optics, rotational motion, and modern physics.
Problem-solving, individually and in groups, is a significant component of the course.
Students are expected to be highly proficient in mathematical skills.
Students will take the AP Physics 2 exam in May.
The prerequisite for AP Physics 12 is AP Physics 11.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Physics 2 Honours 12.

records.title: AP Psychology 12
facts: AP Psychology 12 is an elective course for Grade 12 students.
This course focuses on the systematic and scientific study of human behavior and mental processes.
Major units of study include biological bases of behavior, cognition, development, learning, social psychology, personality, and mental and physical health.
Students apply psychological concepts and research methods to evaluate claims and communicate ideas.
Students will write the AP Psychology exam in May.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Psychology 12.

records.title: AP Research 12
facts: AP Research 12 is an elective Advanced Placement course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
This course prepares students to conduct original university-level research in any discipline.
Students design, plan, and implement a year-long investigation to address a research question.
It builds on skills from AP Seminar, focusing on research methodology, ethical practices, and information analysis.
The course culminates in an academic paper of 4,000–5,000 words and a presentation with an oral defense.
A prerequisite for AP Research 12 is an AP score of at least 3 in AP Seminar 11.
Successful completion awards Ministry Credit for AP Capstone Research 12.

records.title: AP Seminar 11
facts: AP Seminar 11 is an elective Advanced Placement course for Grade 10 and Grade 11 students.
The course focuses on building high-level reading, thinking, discussion, and research skills.
Students explore contemporary issues and pursue academically rigorous research in areas of personal interest.
It involves collaborative discussions, in-depth research papers, persuasive writing, and public speaking.
This course is suitable for students with strong foundations in close reading and scholarly writing.
Students will write the AP Seminar exam in May.
Successful completion awards Ministry Credit for AP Capstone Seminar 11.

records.title: AP Spanish Language 12
facts: AP Spanish Language 12 is a Grade 12 Advanced Placement elective course in Languages.
The course emphasizes communication through interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational skills in real-life situations.
Students develop language skills and learn about Hispanic culture through listening, reading, writing, oral communication, and novel studies.
The course includes analysis of authentic audiovisual resources to enhance understanding of real-world language use.
Students will take the AP Spanish Language and Culture exam in May.
The course is recommended for students who have completed Spanish 12, those with significant Spanish immersion experience, and native speakers.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for AP Spanish Language 12.

records.title: AP Studio Art 11
facts: AP Studio Art 11 is an elective Advanced Placement course for Grade 11 students.
The course challenges students to research, define, produce, assess, refine, and reflect on a body of work in art and/or design.
It is studio-based, requiring active, self-guided studio work during academic class time and an art afternoon commitment.
Instruction includes broad assignments, individual coaching, and guided group critique.
The final AP exam for AP Studio Art 12 is an adjudicated portfolio submission, typically completed in Grade 12.
Ministry credit for Art Studio 11 is awarded at the end of the second year in the course, upon completion of the AP portfolio submission.
Prerequisites include an application, portfolio submission, and an interview with the course instructor, Ms. Andersen.
Students should be passionate about art-making, comfortable in a studio, and capable of self-directed, inquiry-based learning, with several hours per week of independent studio work.

records.title: AP Studio Art 12
facts: AP Studio Art 12 is a Grade 12 elective course.
Students research, define, produce, assess, refine, and reflect on a body of work in art and/or design.
The course is studio-based, requiring active, self-guided studio work during academic class time and an art afternoon commitment.
Instruction includes broadly defined assignments, individual coaching, and guided group critique.
The final AP exam is an adjudicated portfolio submission.
Students starting in Grade 11 typically spend a second year in Grade 12 to submit their AP portfolio.
Ministry credit is awarded at the end of the second year with the completion of the AP portfolio submission.
Prerequisites include an application, portfolio submission, and interview with Ms. Andersen, or completion of AP Studio Art 11.
Ministry credit awarded is AP 2-D Design Portfolio 12 plus Art Studio 12.

records.title: AP World History 12
facts: AP World History: Modern is an elective course for Grade 11 and 12 students.
The course investigates significant events, individuals, developments, and processes from 1200 to the present.

Students develop skills in analyzing primary and secondary sources, developing historical arguments, making historical connections, and reasoning about comparison, causation, and continuity and change over time.
The course explores six themes: humans and the environment; cultural developments and interactions; governance; economic systems; social interactions and organization; and technology and innovation.
Students will write the AP World History Modern exam in May.
It is recommended, but not required, that students complete a regular senior social studies course before taking this course.

records.title: Acting & Drama Program
facts: The Acting & Drama program is taking a creative pause for the 2026 school year.
Brentwood offers introductory and advanced drama courses.
Courses focus on technical skill development, ensemble work, and collaboration.
Junior Drama includes scene studies and character analyses.
Senior Drama explores theatrical technique and theatre history.
Students can participate in the Senior Play and Brentwood Theatre Production, learning about lighting, props, and microphones.
Recent productions include "Puffs," "She Kills Monsters," "7 Stories," "All I Really Need to Know I Learned in Kindergarten," and "Ms. Holmes and Ms. Watson – Apt 2B."

records.title: Advanced Design 12
facts: Advanced Design 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course focuses on design principles, moving from 'making' to 'thinking' about why things are made, their impact, and how design shapes behavior and society.
Students will produce portfolio-quality work and develop professional habits like project management and documentation.
The course emphasizes responsible and sustainable making, considering environmental impact, accessibility, and ethical design decisions.
A recommended prerequisite is a prior design-based course.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Graphic Production 12.

records.title: Advanced Placement (AP) Courses
facts: Brentwood College School offers Advanced Placement (AP) courses designed by the US-based College Board.
These courses provide a curriculum equivalent to first-year university-level courses.
Over 1,000 post-secondary institutions in the USA and Canada grant advanced placement or first-year course credit for AP exam results of 4 or higher.
AP exams occur in the first two weeks of May, and students commit to writing the exam by enrolling in the course.
AP Biology and AP Chemistry begin in Grade 11 and are completed in Grade 12.

records.title: Advanced Placement (AP) Courses
facts: AP courses are first-year university equivalents, administered by CollegeBoard, with May exams graded 1-5.
Scores of 4 or 5 may grant university credit; some global schools require AP for admission.
AP exam participation is mandatory for all AP courses with an exam.

records.title: Advanced Rock Band
facts: For students demonstrating instrument proficiency via audition, focusing on analysis, practical skills, audio, composition, and performance, with emphasis on the current music scene.
Members explore A/V equipment for performance and recording.
Instruction covers band etiquette, instrument roles, microphone technique, balance, blend, mixing, lead/harmony singing, dynamics, and showmanship.

records.title: Advanced Topics in Math 12
facts: Advanced Topics in Math 12 is an elective course for Grade 12 students.
The course covers linear algebra, Calculus II, and number theory, and explores mathematical proof.
Students use tools like Desmos, GeoGebra, and matrix calculators to solve complex problems.
This course is recommended for students pursuing math-intensive post-secondary studies, including engineering, computer science, physics, chemistry, finance, and actuarial science.
The prerequisite is Pre-Calculus 12 with at least Proficient or Extending, and Calculus 12 completed or concurrent.
Upon completion, students receive AP Calculus BC 12 Ministry Credit.

records.title: Anatomy & Physiology 12
facts: Anatomy & Physiology 12 is an elective science course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course examines biological processes from the molecular to the organismal level, including biological molecules, metabolism, and enzymes.
Topics include how the body regulates its internal environment, transports materials across cell membranes, DNA replication, and gene expression.
Students investigate the role of proteins in cell structure and function, principles of genomics and biotechnology, and organ systems.
The course emphasizes the connection between microscopic processes and larger biological organization, and the interdependence of organ systems in maintaining homeostasis.
Chemistry 11 completed or concurrent is recommended as a prerequisite.
Upon completion, students receive Anatomy and Physiology 12 Ministry Credit.

records.title: Art Foundation
facts: Art Foundation is offered to students in Grades 10, 11, and 12.
This course is designed for beginners.
Students develop ideas and creative/critical thinking through assignments addressing the visual language of Art and Design.
Topics may include painting, graphic design, photography, digital imaging, and drawing.
Assignments are linked to 20th-century art history.
Ministry credit is awarded for Art Studio 10, 11, or 12.

Grades 10-12 students must take one arts course and either a second arts course or Rowing.
Further arts courses are possible if space permits after September.
