records.title: Athletics Course Selection Process
facts: Students pre-select their sport courses for the fall term.
Selections for winter and spring sports occur later in the school year.
Students should indicate their top two (junior) or three (senior) sport choices.
It is rare that first or second preferences cannot be offered.
Mr. Blake Gage can be contacted for questions or clarification regarding athletics.
Fall Term Athletics selections are collected using Google Forms, requiring a Brentwood Google Account login.

records.title: Available Arts Courses
facts: Courses include 3D Art & Sculpture, 3D Pottery, AP Music Theory 12, Art Foundation, Broadcast, Competitive Dance, Creative Advocacy Leadership, Dance (Advanced, Beginner, Intermediate), Debate & Model United Nations, Drama, Drama: Film and Stage (Grades 9/10), Drawing & Painting, Filmmaking, Fine Art Photography, Grade 9 Art Rotation, Graphic Art & Design, Hand Built Pottery, Jazz Band, Media Production, Model United Nations & Public Speaking, Musical Theatre, Photography (Advanced Traditional Film, Beginner Traditional Film, Digital), Photojournalism, Rhythm & Blues Band, Robotics, Rock Band, Scientific Illustration, Senior Play, Sport Dance, String Ensemble, Studio Arts Rotation, Theatre Company, Theatre Production, Vocal Ensemble, Wind Ensemble, Woodworking, and Yearbook.

records.title: Available Private Music Instruction Programs
facts: Programs include Classical Piano (RCM), Jazz Piano (Grade 5 RCM equivalent), Classical Voice (RCM), Vocal Jazz, Musical Theatre/Pop Voice, Classical Guitar (RCM), Rock Guitar/Other Strings (banjo, mandolin), Violin, Viola, Cello, Fiddle (RCM Strings), Woodwind/Brass, Percussion/Drum Kit, Harp, and Bagpipes.
Theory tuition is available for all grades.
RCM music programs are recognized by BC Schools for Grade 11/12 Fine Arts Credit with specific co-requisites.

records.title: Beginner French
facts: Beginner French is an elective course for Grade 10 and Grade 11 students with no prior French knowledge.
This intensive course covers essential learning standards from Grades 5 to 10.
The course aims to equip learners with communication skills necessary to take French 11.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Core French Introductory 11.

records.title: Beginner Mandarin
facts: Beginner Mandarin is an elective course for Grade 9, Grade 10, and Grade 11 students.
The course develops listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in a Mandarin-rich environment.
Language acquisition is fostered through storytelling and classroom discussions.

Cultural exploration is a key component, including activities like making bubble tea, crafting mooncakes, writing Spring Couplets, traditional paper-cutting, and a field trip to Victoria's Chinatown for Lunar New Year.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Introductory Mandarin 11.

records.title: Beginner Rock Band
facts: For beginner musicians, this course covers practical skills, audio, composition, and performance, emphasizing popular music history from the 1960s to present.
Students learn basic reading, chord charts, and styles like blues, rock, pop, Motown, reggae, country, and rap.
Instruction includes A/V equipment (PA systems, amps, recording), band etiquette, instrument roles, microphone technique, and showmanship.
The band performs at various venues, including festivals and the Brentwood International Regatta.

records.title: Beginner Spanish
facts: Beginner Spanish is an elective course offered to students in Grade 10 and Grade 11.
This course is designed for students with limited or no prior Spanish knowledge.
It is an intensive course that covers essential learning standards from Grades 5 to 10.
Successful completion of this course prepares students for Spanish 11.
Upon completion, students receive credit for Introductory Spanish 11.

records.title: Boathouse Course
facts: Open to Grades 10-12, no prior rowing experience needed.
Satisfies BC Ministry of Education's Power Technology 10 curriculum.
Scheduled Arts Days (Mon/Wed/Fri) in Arts Block 1, with potential activities at other times.

records.title: Broadcast
facts: The Broadcast course involves students in a dynamic team that documents Brentwood community activities through video, podcasting, and livestreaming.
Available roles include camera operator, editor, livestream producer, host, reporter, and announcer.
Students will schedule event coverage throughout the school year with the instructor.
A computer (preferably Mac) is required for this course, while video equipment is provided by the school.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Media Arts 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Calculus 12
facts: Calculus 12 is a Grade 12 elective course.
The course explores rates of change, accumulated change, instantaneous rates of change, and the behaviors of functions.
Students solve problems using algebra, graphs, and technology.
A strong foundation in Pre-Calculus 11 is necessary for success.
Students can only take one of Calculus 12 and AP Calculus AB 12.
The course prerequisite is Pre-Calculus 12, which must be completed concurrently at least.
Ministry credit is awarded for Calculus 12.

records.title: Career Life Connections
facts: Career Life Connections is a Grade 12 course designed to help students identify and develop personal interests, passions, and goals.
Students reflect on learning experiences and competency development in school and community settings.
The course explores roles and possibilities in personal, educational, and work-life contexts.
It facilitates community networking and experiential learning to support decision-making.
Students design and produce a graduation Capstone project.
Each module includes lessons, assignments, and a Capstone project presented to the student's Advisor.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Career Life Connections.

records.title: Career Life Education
facts: Career Life Education is a Grade 10 course.
The course aims to develop self-directed individuals who set goals, make thoughtful decisions, and take responsibility for pursuing their goals.
It provides relevant, experiential learning opportunities to connect school learning with the working world and societal expectations.
Students develop skills, attitudes, and behaviors to manage their lives, enhance personal well-being, and realize their full potential.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Career Life Education.

records.title: Chemistry 11
facts: Chemistry 11 is an elective science course for Grade 11 students.
Topics include atoms and molecules, matter and energy, the mole, solubility, and organic chemistry.
The course emphasizes laboratory-based learning to develop skills in experimental design, techniques, data analysis, conceptual modelling, and scientific communication.
Proficiency in Science 10 and Math 10 is highly recommended as a prerequisite.
Students receive credit for Chemistry 11 upon completion.

records.title: Chemistry 12
facts: Chemistry 12 is a Grade 12 elective science course.
Main units include Reaction Kinetics, Dynamic Equilibrium, Solubility, Acids & Bases, and Electrochemistry.

The course requires strong skills in reading dense word problems, writing specific descriptions of theory, and navigating a scientific calculator for exponential notation, orders of operations, and base 10 logarithms.
Assessments typically involve quizzes, lab reports, and cumulative or unit tests throughout the year.
The prerequisite for Chemistry 12 is Chemistry 11, with a final mark of 80% in Chemistry 11 highly recommended.

records.title: Coding 11: Python
facts: Coding 11: Python is an elective course available to Grade 10 and Grade 11 students.
This course is designed for beginners new to coding.
Classroom activities are project-based, focusing on problem-solving and combining online learning with hands-on coding challenges.
It is suitable for students who enjoy problem-solving, have strong math skills, and are curious.
Upon completion, students receive credit for Computer Science 11.

records.title: Comparative Cultures 12
facts: Comparative Cultures 12 is an elective Social Studies course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course provides an understanding of the accomplishments of past global civilizations.
It examines how cultural diversity deepens understanding of others and how belief systems, social structures, and language shape artistic expression.
The course also explores how geographic factors influence the evolution of agriculture, trade, and complex societies.

records.title: Composition Rock Band
facts: For students with one year of Advanced Rock Band or audition proficiency, this class teaches composing, arranging, and recording music, including computer and music-scoring software.
Students explore, compose, and perform styles like blues, rock, pop, Motown, reggae, country, and rap.
The band performs throughout the year at various venues, including festivals and the Brentwood International Regatta.
Awards Ministry Credit for Composition & Production 11, 12.

records.title: Contemporary Indigenous Studies 12
facts: Contemporary Indigenous Studies 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
This course fulfills both the Indigenous Studies and senior Social Studies graduation requirements.
It covers contemporary Indigenous cultures, societies, and historical, political, and social topics.
The course focuses on developing an informed understanding of the relationship between Indigenous and non-Indigenous Canadians.
Learning involves experiential tasks, class discussions, novel reading, group projects, and current events.
Students receive credit for Contemporary Indigenous Studies 12 upon completion.

records.title: Course Options
facts: Brentwood offers a wide variety of courses.
Students are encouraged to explore options in academics, arts, and athletics.

records.title: Course Selection Changes & Online Courses
facts: Course changes are possible until spring break via form; after, contact University Counselling.
New students contact Mr.
Rodrigues for changes; returning students by July 15.

records.title: Creative Advocacy Leadership
facts: Creative Advocacy Leadership is a Media Arts course.
The course focuses on developing effective leadership and creative problem-solving skills.
Students will use creative media to inform, motivate, and activate communities to address issues.
Topics for advocacy include the environment, gender, race, and wellness.
The course aims to empower students to improve their local and global communities.
Upon completion, students receive a Board-Authorized credit, which is to be confirmed.

records.title: Creative Writing 12
facts: Creative Writing 12 is an elective English course for Grade 12 students interested in developing their writing skills.
Students refine their ability to write in complex, controlled styles across various genres, including screenwriting, short stories, and poetry.
This course is not classroom-based; students receive monthly tasks and manage their own schedules.
Creative Writing 12 cannot replace English 12 for post-secondary admissions and requires an application for enrollment.

records.title: Dance: Advanced
facts: The Advanced Dance course focuses on technique, combinations, stamina, strength, artistry, and performance.
Students in this class concentrate on the technical aspects of ballet, pointe prep, tap, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, and acrobatics.
This course is suitable for dancers with 7 or more years of dance experience.
Ministry credits awarded include Dance 9, Dance Company 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Dance: Beginner
facts: The Beginner Dance course focuses on vocabulary, proper placement, and body awareness.
Students learn the fundamentals of ballet, tap, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, and acrobatics.
This class is suitable for dancers with 0-4 years of dance experience.
Ministry credits awarded include Dance Foundations 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Dance: Intermediate
facts: The Intermediate Dance course helps students incorporate basic movements and steps into combinations to develop stronger dancing skills.
Dancers explore the technical aspects of ballet, pointe prep, tap, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, and acrobatics.
This class is suitable for dancers with 4-7 years of dance experience.
Ministry credits awarded include Dance Technique & Performance 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Debate & Model United Nations
facts: Debate & Model United Nations is an Arts course with multiple components.
It is designed for students to improve communication skills, weigh conflicting truth claims, and craft arguments.
Students of all experience levels receive support for small-group settings and national competitions.
All students participate in debate activities and can specialize in areas for external competitions.
The Model United Nations component enhances formal communication skills and prepares students for various speaking experiences.
Speaking skills covered include poetry recitation, interpretive reading, impromptu speaking, persuasive speaking, interview strategies, and after-dinner speaking.
Students learn to deliver ideas with confidence, focusing on projection, enunciation, modulation, pace, and tone.
The Model United Nations component allows students to debate contemporary and historical issues from international perspectives.
Students can participate in conferences such as BMUN, ShawMUN, VMUN, NHSMUN, and SSUNS.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Debate & Model UN 10, 11, or 12.

records.title: Design 11
facts: Design 11 is an elective course for Grade 10 students.
This course explores creative and practical applications of design across multiple disciplines, including interior design, graphic design, costuming, and event planning.
Students develop foundational skills in design principles, visual communication, and project execution.
Topics include spatial planning, color theory, typography, fabric selection, and thematic event coordination.
The course emphasizes creativity, problem-solving, and collaboration.
Students with strong visual arts skills may find this beneficial for the course.

records.title: Drama: Introduction to Acting and Drama
facts: The 'Introduction to Acting and Drama' course is designed for self-discovery and developing essential life skills.
Students engage in expressive exercises and explore foundational elements of acting.
The course helps students discover dynamic acting techniques, enhance communication, boost confidence, and express emotions.
It provides a welcoming environment for students to build connections and engage in artistic expression.
Students can develop skills for confident movement and stage presence.
Ministry credit awarded is Drama 10.

records.title: Drawing & Painting
facts: This course focuses on strengthening technical and observational skills in drawing and painting.
Students will explore various techniques and subject matter, building on fundamentals of composition, light, tone, and colour.
Topics include life drawing, portraiture, landscape, still life, perspective, composition, and abstraction.
Students will use a range of materials and techniques to improve their skills and produce artwork for two major exhibitions.
Ministry credits awarded are Studio Arts 2D 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Earth Sciences 11
facts: Earth Sciences 11 is an elective science course for Grade 10 and Grade 11 students.
The course focuses on understanding scientific principles related to earth systems and exploring sustainable solutions.
Students learn the basics of astronomy, geology, hydrology, oceanography, and atmospheric sciences.
The curriculum includes an understanding of Indigenous perspectives on earth systems and their connections with the solar system.
This course is designed for students interested in earth and space sciences, sustainability, and learning both in and outside the classroom.

records.title: Economics 12
facts: Economics 12 is an elective Social Studies course available to Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course explores economic theory, including macro- and micro-economics, and the structure of the Canadian economic system.
Students investigate the 'economic problem' of satisfying unlimited wants with limited resources.
The curriculum covers the ideas of economists such as Smith, Ricardo, and Marx, and contemporary economic paradigms.

records.title: Engineering 11: Advanced Design
facts: Engineering 11: Advanced Design is an elective course that expands on design principles.
The course focuses on critical thinking, responsible creation, and navigating complex real-world problems.
Students will produce portfolio-quality work and develop professional habits like project management and documentation.
The course emphasizes responsible and sustainable making, considering environmental impact, accessibility, and ethical design.
A recommended prerequisite is a prior design-based course.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Graphic Production 12.

records.title: English 10
facts: English 10 is a Grade 10 course where students are concurrently enrolled in Literary Studies 10 and Composition 10.
Students will engage with independent reading and assigned texts including nonfiction, novels, short fiction, verse, and Shakespeare.
Frequent writing assignments cover various styles, focusing on expository essays, synthesis, and journalism.

The year-long course concludes with a four-week genre studies unit, allowing students to explore specialized topics like romance novels, Stephen King, David Sedaris, children's literature, or photojournalism.
Ministry Credit awarded includes 2 credits for Literary Studies 10 and 2 credits for Composition 10.

records.title: English 11
facts: English 11 is an academic course for Grade 11 students.
Students explore themes, periods, authors, or global areas through literary works and various media.
The course aims to increase literacy skills through close reading of challenging texts.
Focus areas for written composition include narrative, expository, descriptive, persuasive, and opinion pieces.
Students will practice planning, drafting, and editing for specific audiences and disciplines.
The course also covers citing sources, assessing evidence credibility, and evaluating source quality.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for Literary Studies 11.

records.title: English 12
facts: English 12, or English Studies 12, is a Grade 12 course designed to build upon and extend students' prior learning in English.
The course aims to refine students' communication skills in various contexts and enhance their critical and creative thinking about language.
Students will explore texts and literature from diverse sources, modes, and worldviews.
The curriculum helps students deepen their understanding of themselves and others in a changing world.
Students will compose various written responses, including expository, synthesis, and literary analysis essays.
Ministry Credit is awarded for English Studies 12.

records.title: English 9
facts: English 9 is a foundational Grade 9 language course focused on building essential literacy and communication skills.
Students will engage in independent reading and study assigned nonfiction prose, novels, short fiction, and verse.
The course introduces students to the writing process, with approximately weekly writing assignments in various styles.
Particular attention is given to artistic description, the expository paragraph, and the keyhole essay.

records.title: English First Peoples 10
facts: English First Peoples 10 is a Grade 10 English course that fulfills the Indigenous Studies graduation requirement.
Students investigate oral traditions and the function of storytelling in communication, art, and culture.
The course explores First Peoples' principles of learning and includes a genre studies unit where students complete a passion project.
Upon completion, students receive 2 credits for EFP Literary Studies 10 and 2 credits for EFP New Media 10.

records.title: English First Peoples 12
facts: English First Peoples 12 is a Grade 12 academic course that fulfills the Indigenous Studies graduation requirement.
Students will engage with sophisticated texts of literary merit and complete challenging assignments.
The course incorporates First Peoples' principles of learning and recognizes the value of First Peoples' culture and oral traditions.
Learning materials include oral, audio, visual, cinematic, electronic media, novels, and non-fiction books from authentic First Peoples' voices.

records.title: Entrepreneurship 12
facts: Entrepreneurship 12 is an elective course available to Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course covers both theoretical and practical aspects of entrepreneurship.
Students will propose, develop, and run a small business for a brief period.
Later in the year, students will develop and implement a larger business venture during the annual Brentwood Regatta in April.

The BC Ministry of Education labels this course as an Applied Skill, which may not be accepted for admission by many Canadian universities; students should consult University Counselling for more information.

records.title: Film Studies 12
facts: Film Studies 12 is an elective Grade 12 English course.
The course focuses on visual storytelling, filmmaking principles, and advanced criticism and theory.
Learning involves screenings, readings, discussions, and written responses.
Students will investigate the work of screenwriters, directors, and theorists to understand film's historical and contemporary context.
The course aims to refine students' ability to understand, critique, and articulate cinematic significance.
Film Studies 12 is offered as an evening seminar, once per week.
Upon completion, students receive Ministry Credit for New Media 12.

records.title: Filmmaking
facts: The Filmmaking course explores the art of filmmaking from pre-production to post-production.
Students will participate in simulated pitching sessions and table reads, and will shoot and edit their own films.
Specialization pathways available include cinematography, editing, effects, producing, scriptwriting, directing, and performing for the screen.
Students manage film sets through skill-building activities and projects.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Film & Television 11 and 12.

records.title: Financial Accounting 12
facts: Financial Accounting 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
Students will master basic accounting principles and cycles, and learn to implement internal control systems for business management.
The course covers evaluating a company's financial health through statement analysis and understanding stock market terminology.
Learning is heavily emphasized through case studies, initially focusing on building financial statements and later on analysis and critical thinking.
Strong math and organizational skills are beneficial for this course.

The BC Ministry of Education labels this course as an Applied Skill, which may affect its acceptance for admission at some Canadian universities; students should consult University Counselling for more information.

records.title: Foundations of Mathematics 12
facts: Foundations of Mathematics 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course builds understanding in graphs, probability, statistics, finance, and geometry.
Projects are based on real-world applications such as mortgage calculations, stock market investing, and data trend analysis.
Students are introduced to online applications for managing finances and creating math-based art.

records.title: French 10
facts: French 10 is an academic course for Grade 10 students.
The course develops reading and listening comprehension, creative writing, and oral expression.
Students explore cultures and perspectives from Francophone countries.
Assessments include individual work and collaborative projects.
Learning is supported through interactive stories and novels that incorporate core grammatical structures.
French is used as the primary language of instruction.
The prerequisite for French 10 is French 9 or equivalent.

records.title: French 11
facts: French 11 is a Grade 11 language course focusing on reading, writing, speaking, and listening.
The course uses an acquisition-based approach, emphasizing natural language development.
Activities include novel studies, cultural explorations, personal and formal writing, interactive games, and dictées.
French is the primary language of interaction and instruction.
A prerequisite for French 11 is French 10 or its equivalent.
Upon completion, students receive Core French 11 Ministry Credit.

records.title: French 12
facts: French 12 is a Grade 12 elective language course.
It targets all areas of language competency: reading, writing, speaking, and listening.
The course uses an acquisition-based approach, focusing on natural language development.
Learning activities include novel studies, cultural investigations, personal and formal writing, interactive games, and dictées.
Students extend learning beyond the classroom through experiences like cooking classes and visits to a local French Immersion elementary school.
The prerequisite for French 12 is French 11 or its equivalent.
Upon completion, students receive Core French 12 Ministry Credit.

records.title: French 9
facts: French 9 is a Grade 9 language course designed for both beginners and students with prior French instruction.
The course emphasizes listening, speaking, and writing skills, along with grammatical understanding.
Students are exposed to French through storytelling to facilitate language acquisition.
Students who have studied a Romance language (Latin, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, or Romanian) may find this course suitable.

records.title: Grade 10 Academic Course Selection Process
facts: Academic course selections for Grade 10 are submitted via Google Forms.
Students must log in using their Brentwood Google Account to access the selection process.

records.title: Grade 10 Courses
facts: Grade 10 encourages exploration with electives for advanced study. The curriculum integrates Planning 10, covering post-secondary planning, organizational skills, health/career education, and financial literacy.

records.title: Grade 10 Elective Courses
facts: Grade 10 students must select one elective.
Options include AP Seminar 11, Beginner French/Mandarin/Spanish, Coding 11: Python, Design 11, Earth Science 11, Marketing & Promotion 11, or other appropriate Grade 11 electives.
Students need to demonstrate suitability for advanced Grade 11/12 electives.

records.title: Grade 10 English, Science, and Language Options
facts: Grade 10 English options are English 10 and English First Peoples 10.
Science options include Science 10, Science 10: Sustainable Engineering, and Geology 12.
Core language courses are French 10, Mandarin 10, and Spanish 10.

records.title: Grade 10 Required Academic Courses
facts: Grade 10 students must enroll in English 10 (or English First Peoples 10), Mathematics 10, Social Studies 10, Science 10, and a Language 10.
Advanced students can take the next course in a sequence.

records.title: Grade 10, 11 & 12 Arts Course Requirements
facts: Grades 10-12 students must enroll in one arts course.
They must also enroll in a second arts course or Rowing.

records.title: Grade 11 Course Options
facts: English options: AP English 11, English 11.
Math options: Foundations of Mathematics 12, Pre-Calculus 11.

records.title: Grade 11 Course Requirements
facts: Grade 11 students typically take six academic courses.
BC graduation requires Grade 11 Language Arts, Grade 11/12 Math, Grade 11/12 Science, and a Senior Social Studies course.

records.title: Grade 11 Courses
facts: Grade 11 involves university planning, with elective choices impacting Grade 12 and post-secondary. This 'pre-AP' year builds a foundation for Grade 12 AP exams, with some electives offering AP exam possibilities in Grade 11.

records.title: Grade 12 Academic Course Requirements
facts: Grade 12 students must select five academic courses, including English Studies 12, to meet BC graduation requirements and post-secondary admissions.
A minimum of four electives are required.
Taking six courses is possible if committed for the full year.

records.title: Grade 12 Courses
facts: Grade 12 builds skills for post-secondary journeys. Electives include numerous Advanced Placement (AP) options, potentially earning first-year university credit. Support is provided by peers, advisors, and counsellors.

records.title: Grade 12 Elective Options
facts: Grade 12 students select four electives.

Options include 20th Century World History 12, Advanced Design 12, Anatomy & Physiology 12, AP Biology 12, AP Calculus AB 12, AP Chemistry 12, AP Computer Science A 12, AP French Language 12, AP Physics 12, Calculus 12, Chemistry 12, Creative Writing 12, Economics 12, Financial Accounting 12, French 12, Law Studies 12, Mandarin 12, Physics 12, Pre-Calculus 12, Spanish 12, and Statistics 12.

records.title: Grade 12 English Options
facts: Grade 12 students must choose one English option from: English Studies 12, English First Peoples 12, Literary Studies 12, or AP English Literature & Composition 12.
Literary Studies 12 or AP English Literature & Composition 12 also grant credit for English Studies 12.

records.title: Grade 9 Academic Course Descriptions
facts: Academic courses available for Grade 9 include Beginner Mandarin, English 9, French 9, Mathematics 9, Metamorphosis 9, and Spanish 9.

records.title: Grade 9 Academic Course Selection Process
facts: Academic course selections are collected using Google Forms.
Students must log in with their Brentwood Google Account to begin the selection process.

records.title: Grade 9 Art Rotation
facts: The Grade 9 Art Rotation provides an opportunity for students to experience various arts.
Students rotate through three different arts each term in block one of the arts afternoons: 2-D Art Foundations, Drama, and 3-D Art.
Projects in these arts aim to cultivate creativity and self-expression.
After the rotation, Grade 9 students can select another art or rowing to complete their arts afternoon.
Students who play woodwind, brass, or percussion instruments can opt out of the rotation to join the Wind Ensemble.

records.title: Grade 9 Arts Course Requirements
facts: Grade 9 students must enroll in either Arts Rotation or String Ensemble.
They must also enroll in one arts course or Rowing.

records.title: Grade 9 Courses
facts: Grade 9 focuses on metacognition and foundational learning. Core courses are English 9, Mathematics 9, and Metamorphosis 9 (creative, STEM, collaborative). Language options include Beginner Mandarin, French 9, and Spanish 9.

records.title: Grade 9 Required Academic Courses
facts: Every Grade 9 student is enrolled in English 9, Mathematics 9, Metamorphosis 9, and a Language 9.
Metamorphosis 9 combines Science 9, Social Studies 9, and Applied Design, Skills & Technology 9.
Students who are advanced in Math 9 (e.g., completed in Grade 8) can select the next math course in the sequence if the timetable allows.
New students with a strong background in French, Mandarin, or Spanish can take a higher-level course suited to their skills.
The Modern Languages Department will assess new students to confirm the appropriate language course level.

records.title: Grade 9 and 10 Sport Options
facts: Grade 9 and 10 sport options are intentionally limited during the first week of school to provide team-building opportunities for junior students.
Additional senior sport options may become available after the first week if students wish to change or if coaching staff deem it appropriate.
Students have the opportunity to try sports and change their choice, provided they do not delay too long.

records.title: Graphic Art & Design
facts: This course is for students interested in digital art and design.
Students will learn and work with Adobe Creative Suite programs like Illustrator and Photoshop.
Topics include image development, graphic design, advertising, digital photography, and book arts.
Projects will be both collaborative and individual.
Students will have the opportunity to build a digital art portfolio.
Ministry credits awarded are Media Design 10, Graphic Arts 11, and 12.

records.title: Hand Built Pottery
facts: This course teaches a range of hand-building techniques including pinching, coil building, slab construction, sculpture, and glazing.
Students will learn decorative surface techniques.
The curriculum includes a review or introduction to the elements and principles of design, historical and contemporary developments in ceramics, and art critiques.
Students are encouraged to experiment with materials and develop personal flair in their work.
Ministry credits awarded are Studio Arts 3D 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Human Geography 12
facts: Human Geography 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course explores how data analysis helps understand the globally connected world.
Students examine how demographic and physical features, natural resources, and human activities shape population distribution and alter landscapes.
The course highlights the complex relationships between people and their environments.
Learning activities include group discussions, reading analyses, and guided and self-directed inquiry projects.
Upon completion, students receive Human Geography 12 Ministry Credit.

records.title: Jazz Band
facts: The Brentwood Jazz Band is open to students with intermediate to advanced musicianship.
The band plays moderately challenging jazz arrangements.
Rhythm section, brass, reeds musicians, and vocalists are all welcome.
A high priority is placed on ear training and sight-reading skills, as well as improvisation.
The band performs both on and off campus, including at music festivals.
In 2024, the Jazz Band received Gold at the Con Brio Whistler Mountain Music Festival and Silver at the West Coast Jazz Festival, earning an invitation to Nationals in 2025.
Ministry credits awarded are Instrumental Music: Jazz Band 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Law Studies 12
facts: Law Studies 12 is an elective course offered to Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course provides exposure to the fundamentals of Canadian Law.
Topics include criminal law, torts, contracts, constitutional law, human rights, Aboriginal law, and family law.
Students develop critical thinking, problem-solving, written, and oral advocacy skills.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Law Studies 12.

records.title: Life Sciences 11
facts: Life Sciences 11 is an elective science course for Grade 11 students.
The course provides an understanding of the interconnectedness of life on Earth, exploring what defines life, its organization, and the role of evolution.
Students examine prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and investigate single-celled and multicellular life forms.
The curriculum includes the science of classification, microscopic environments, bacteria, non-living viruses, and their impacts on health.
An in-depth study of evolution by natural selection, including contributions from Darwin, is a key component.
The course concludes with a focused study of ecology and relationships among organisms and their environments.

records.title: Literary Studies 12
facts: Literary Studies 12 is an English course for Grade 12 students.
The course focuses on in-depth exploration of language and literature through various themes, periods, authors, or global regions.
Students will analyze literary works (fiction and non-fiction) and different media.
The curriculum emphasizes close reading, written composition (narrative, expository, descriptive, persuasive, opinion), source citation, and evaluation of evidence.
This course cannot be used as a substitute for English 12 for post-secondary admissions.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Literary Studies 12.

records.title: Mandarin 10
facts: Mandarin 10 is a language course for Grade 10 students.
The course builds on language competencies in listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
It fosters language acquisition through storytelling, classroom discussions, and an immersive environment.
Cultural activities include making bubble tea, crafting mooncakes, writing Spring Couplets, traditional paper-cutting, and a field trip to Victoria's Chinatown for Lunar New Year.
A prerequisite for Mandarin 10 is Beginner Mandarin or equivalent, requiring at least one year of Mandarin studies.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Mandarin 10.

records.title: Mandarin 11
facts: Mandarin 11 is a language course for Grade 11 students.
The course aims to enhance confidence, communication, and trust in an interactive Mandarin environment.
It covers listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills, fostered through storytelling and discussions.
Students share about daily life and future plans.
Cultural exploration includes making bubble tea, crafting mooncakes, writing Spring Couplets, traditional paper-cutting, and a field trip to Victoria's Chinatown for Lunar New Year.
A prerequisite for Mandarin 11 is Mandarin 10 or equivalent, requiring at least two years of Mandarin studies.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Mandarin 11.

records.title: Mandarin 12
facts: Mandarin 12 is a Grade 12 elective course that focuses on developing reading, writing, speaking, and listening competencies.
The course emphasizes natural language development through storytelling and classroom discussions.

Cultural exploration is a key component, including activities like making bubble tea, crafting mooncakes, writing Spring Couplets, traditional paper-cutting, and a field trip to Victoria's Chinatown for Lunar New Year.
A prerequisite for Mandarin 12 is Mandarin 11 or its equivalent, requiring at least three years of Mandarin studies.
Students receive Ministry Credit for Mandarin 12 upon completion.

records.title: Marine Sciences 11
facts: Marine Sciences 11 is a Grade 11 elective course.
The course explores ocean ecosystems, the cycles and processes that sustain marine life, and the interaction between life and the aquatic environment.
Students engage in scientific inquiry, research, and project-based learning, including lab exercises and extensive field components.
The course incorporates hands-on experience on and in the water.
Current issues related to the conservation of ocean ecosystems are discussed.
This course grants dual credits for Life Sciences 11 (LFSC 11) and Environmental Science 11 (EVSC 11).

records.title: Marketing & Promotion 11
facts: Marketing & Promotion 11 is a broad, fast-paced elective course for Grade 10 students.
It serves as an introduction to the Grade 12 and AP business courses offered at Brentwood.
Students practice and master skills such as effective group work, keyboarding, business writing, and presenting.
The course covers basic word processing, spreadsheet, and publishing skills using Google, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Products.
Issues such as business etiquette, ethics, and social enterprise are also examined.

records.title: Mathematics 10
facts: Mathematics 10 is a Grade 10 course designed to prepare students for post-secondary programs.
Main topics include algebra, geometry, trigonometry, number operations, and data analysis.
The course emphasizes symbolic manipulation, generalization of mathematical concepts, and formal mathematics.
Mathematical processes such as communication, problem-solving, reasoning, and technology are highlighted.
Students receive Ministry Credit for Foundations of Math & Pre-Calculus 10.

records.title: Mathematics 9
facts: Mathematics 9 is a Grade 9 course that uses problem-based learning to connect math to real-world applications.
The curriculum aims to develop deep mathematical understanding, procedural fluency, logical reasoning, and analytical thinking.
Units of study include operations with rational numbers, exponents and exponent laws, and operations with polynomials.
Other topics covered are two-variable linear relations and equations, spatial proportional reasoning, and statistics in society.

records.title: Mathematics Course Selection Guidance
facts: Pre-Calculus 11 is for Science, Engineering, or Commerce, as it's a prerequisite for Pre-Calculus 12 and Calculus.
Foundations of Mathematics 12 or Statistics 12 suit Arts, Humanities, or Social Sciences.
UBC requires Pre-Calculus 11 or Foundations of Mathematics 12.

records.title: Media Arts Courses
facts: Specific courses offered include Broadcast, Creative Advocacy Leadership, Filmmaking, Graphic Art & Design, Photojournalism, and Yearbook.

records.title: Music Courses
facts: Specific music courses include Jazz Band, Rhythm & Blues Band, Rock Band, String Ensemble, Vocal Ensemble, and Wind Ensemble.

records.title: Musical Theatre
facts: Musical Theatre is a performance course for actors, singers, and dancers.
The course involves a full-length musical supported by professional live musicians on the George Killy Theatre stage.
Class time and Sunday afternoons in the winter term are used for rehearsals.
Principal roles are decided by audition, and those selected will also rehearse on sports afternoons in the winter term.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Musical Theatre 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Philosophy, Politics & Economics 12 (PPE 12)
facts: Philosophy, Politics & Economics 12 (PPE 12) is a Grade 12 elective course.
This course fulfills the senior Social Studies graduation requirement.
It is a seminar-style class designed to challenge students to think critically about complex problems.
The course uses philosophical thought as a foundation to discuss and debate pressing global challenges.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Philosophy 12.

records.title: Photography Courses
facts: Photography courses include Photography: Advanced Traditional Film, Photography: Beginner Traditional Film, and Photography: Digital.
Beginners learn film development in darkrooms, while advanced students explore creative tools and techniques.
Digital photography focuses on capturing, processing, and printing images.

records.title: Photography: Advanced Traditional Film
facts: This course is offered to students in Grades 11 and 12.
A prerequisite for this program is the successful completion of the Beginner Traditional Photography course.
The course explores advanced techniques including specialized films, camera accessories, studio lighting, and advanced darkroom skills.
Students will learn techniques such as multiple exposures, negative sandwiches, contrast control, motion in still images, hand-colouring, and toning.
Students need to bring their own 35mm SLR traditional (film) camera or rent one from the school for $150.
Additional costs apply for film and printing paper, available from the School Store.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Photography 11 and 12.

records.title: Photography: Beginner Traditional Film
facts: This course teaches the art of traditional (analog) photography to both experienced and new photographers.
Students learn camera controls, accessories, photo design, and basic darkroom skills including film processing and paper printing.
Students need to bring their own 35mm SLR traditional (film) camera or rent one from the school for $150.
Additional costs apply for film and printing paper, which are available from the School Store.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Photography 10.

records.title: Photography: Digital
facts: The prerequisite for this course is the successful completion of the Beginner Traditional Film Photography course.
This course transitions students to digital equipment and photo editing using Photoshop and Lightroom.
Students will explore advanced camera creative tools, specialized camera accessories, and an introduction to studio lighting.
Students require a digital SLR camera, a laptop capable of digital photo processing, and a minimum 1-terabyte hard drive.
The school provides Photoshop and Lightroom for editing and has a small selection of digital SLR cameras for rent.
Additional costs apply for printing paper, available from the School Store.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Photography 11 and 12.

records.title: Photojournalism
facts: Photojournalism is a course for students interested in documenting the school year through print and photos.
Students in this course publish news stories about school events fortnightly on the Brentwood website.
Prerequisites include the ability to work independently, meet deadlines, cover assignments outside class time, demonstrate superior written English, and have a proven record of meeting deadlines.
Experience with publishing and an SLR digital camera are considered assets.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Digital Communications 11 and Digital Media Development 12.

records.title: Physics 11
facts: Physics 11 is a Grade 11 science course exploring fundamental principles of motion, forces, energy, and waves.
Students learn to describe, analyze, and predict object motion and understand how forces influence it.
The course examines various forms of energy, emphasizing conservation and its ability to do work.
Mechanical waves and their energy transfer through a medium are also studied.
A strong recommendation for this course is proficiency in Science 10 and Math 10, as the approach is mathematical.
Students receive Ministry Credit for Physics 11 upon completion.

records.title: Physics 12
facts: Physics 12 is a Grade 12 elective science course.
The course covers topics such as vector analysis, relativity, statics, momentum, energy, circular motion, gravitational forces, electrostatics, and electromagnetism.

Main ideas include measurement of motion depending on the frame of reference, forces causing linear and circular motion, forces and energy interactions within fields, and conservation of momentum in a closed system.
The course involves mostly paired or group activities like discussions, exploratory investigations, experimental design, projects, and presentations.
It is a mathematically rigorous course that requires strong math skills and builds on concepts from Physics 11.
The prerequisite for Physics 12 is Physics 11.

records.title: Political Studies 12
facts: Political Studies 12 is an elective course offered to Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course focuses on understanding how political decisions are made to foster informed and engaged citizenship.
It examines how political institutions and ideologies influence the exercise of power and political outcomes.
The curriculum explores decision-making in democratic systems and the impact of political and social power distribution.
Topics include international and Canadian issues, requiring engagement with political philosophy and current-events texts.

Learning activities involve class discussions, portfolios on political issues, analyses of global political issues and philosophies, MUN-style simulations, and political speech analysis and presentations.

records.title: Pottery Program
facts: Students learn to build pots by hand.
They also learn to decorate, glaze, and fire their clay creations.
The program encourages experimentation with materials and developing personal flair.
Instructors for pottery are Robert Burgess and Joe Lyons.

records.title: Pre-Calculus 11
facts: Pre-Calculus 11 is a Grade 11 mathematics course.
The course develops abstract algebra skills, numerical operations, proportional reasoning, and competency with functions.
It builds a foundation for higher mathematics, with skills applicable in science and finance.
The course emphasizes communication, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills in mathematics.
A final mark of at least 73% in Math 10 is highly recommended as a prerequisite for Pre-Calculus 11.

records.title: Pre-Calculus 12
facts: Pre-Calculus 12 is an elective course for Grade 12 students planning further studies in mathematics or sciences.
The course provides a deeper understanding of how quantities change in relation to one another.
It features a rigorous workload and a fast-paced delivery of content.
Students should expect to spend approximately one hour of out-of-class work for each instructional lesson.
A strong foundation in algebra, graphing, functions, and trigonometry is essential for success.
Units of study include limits, derivatives and their applications, and integration and its applications.
Completion of Pre-Calculus 12 is recommended as a prerequisite, or concurrent enrollment.

records.title: Rhythm & Blues Band
facts: The Rhythm & Blues Band is for talented instrumentalists and vocalists.
Students learn R&B arrangements, incorporating rock, gospel, and blues influences.
The band includes a rhythm section, brass, reeds, and vocalists.
Vocalists receive instruction on microphone technique.
The band performs throughout the year both on and off campus, including at the Whistler Mountain Festival and national festivals like MusicFest Canada.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Instrumental Music: Jazz Band 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Robotics
facts: The Robotics course uses VEX Robotics technology.
Students learn about the design, construction, and programming of actively controlled mobile robots and autonomous machines with sensor feedback systems.
Students primarily work in small design teams.
The course aims for students to challenge each other and teams from other schools in various competitions.
Students can choose between Beginner or Experienced options based on their skill level.
Essential skills include internal motivation and problem-solving abilities, along with effective teamwork.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Electronics & Robotics 10, Robotics 11, and 12.

records.title: Science 10
facts: Science 10 is a Grade 10 course providing a broad foundation in science.

The course is divided into four main ideas: energy change during chemical reactions, DNA as the basis for diversity, the law of conservation of energy, and the Big Bang theory explaining the universe's formation and evolution.
In chemistry, students examine chemical reactions, radioactivity, and their applications.
The biology portion focuses on DNA, its function, inheritance, and relation to natural selection and evolution.
Physics topics include quantifying different forms of energy and their transformations, particularly potential to kinetic energy.
Astronomy explores modern observations and historical perspectives on looking at stars.

records.title: Science 10: Sustainable Engineering
facts: Science 10: Sustainable Engineering is a Grade 10 academic course.
It introduces students to sustainable engineering by integrating principles of physics, chemistry, biology, and astronomy, aligned with the Science 10 curriculum.
The course uses project-based learning to teach the basics of the engineering design process.
Students explore sustainability challenges and investigate possible solutions.
This option is designed for students passionate about science, interested in sustainability, comfortable with a faster pace, and open to project-based learning both in and outside the classroom.

records.title: Scientific Illustration
facts: This drawing course integrates science as a theme for artistic study, encouraging visual, literary, and critical thinking.
Students develop technical drawing skills and artistic expression.
They create original artworks based on scientific observation and inquiry.
Students build visual communication skills using both traditional and digital media.
They also analyze historical and contemporary scientific illustrations.
The instructor for this course is Sean Hacker Teper, and coursework inspiration includes sketches from Brentwood's Life Sciences 11.

records.title: Scientific Illustration
facts: Scientific Illustration is an interdisciplinary arts course that integrates science as a theme for artistic study.
The course encourages visual, literary, and critical thinking, bridging the gap for students interested in both art and biological/environmental subjects.
Students will develop technical illustration skills, create original artworks based on scientific observation, and build visual communication skills using traditional and digital media.
The curriculum includes analyzing historical and contemporary scientific illustrations and critical reflection on the creative process.
Upon completion, students can earn Ministry Credit for Studio Art 2D 11 and Studio Art 2D 12.

records.title: Social Justice 12
facts: Social Justice 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students.
The course focuses on the interconnectedness of social justice issues and how individual worldviews influence understanding.
Students examine the causes and impacts of social injustice and the role of social justice initiatives.
Topics include intersectionality, privilege, power, LGBTQ2 issues, Indigenous awareness, and gender equality.
Students are encouraged to challenge their current mindset and adopt a growth mindset.

records.title: Social Studies 10
facts: Social Studies 10 is a Grade 10 course that examines social, political, economic, and global forces from 1918 to the present.
The course explores the influence of political ideologies, institutions, and the effects of domestic and international conflicts.
Students study the development and roles of Canadian, First Nations, and other political systems.
The curriculum addresses the impact of discriminatory policies and historical injustices on populations.
Canada's role as a middle power, its foreign policy, peacekeeping efforts, and international economic relationships are also covered.

records.title: Spanish 10
facts: Spanish 10 is a Grade 10 language course.
Students learn through listening, reading, and writing stories, supported by songs, games, and short videos.
The course incorporates individual and group work, including projects based on novels.
Instruction is primarily in Spanish, using a communicative approach with an emphasis on comprehensible input.
A significant focus is placed on exploring the diverse traditions of the Spanish-speaking world.
The prerequisite for Spanish 10 is Spanish 9 or equivalent.

records.title: Spanish 11
facts: Spanish 11 is a Grade 11 language course that explores the connection between language and culture.
Students develop skills in reading and listening comprehension, creative writing, and oral communication.
The course uses interactive stories and novels to introduce basic grammatical structures.
There is a greater emphasis on Hispanic cultures from around the world.
The prerequisite for Spanish 11 is Spanish 10 or equivalent.

records.title: Spanish 12
facts: Spanish 12 is a Grade 12 elective language course.
The course focuses on improving reading, listening comprehension, writing, and oral communication skills.
Students learn through reading stories and authentic materials, analyzing audiovisual resources, and completing cultural projects.
The course explores the connection between language and culture, offering opportunities to learn about Hispanic cultures worldwide.
The prerequisite for Spanish 12 is Spanish 11 or its equivalent.

records.title: Spanish 9
facts: Spanish 9 is a Grade 9 language course designed for both beginners and students with prior Spanish instruction.
The course emphasizes listening, speaking, and writing skills, along with grammatical understanding.
Students are introduced to Spanish through storytelling to facilitate language acquisition, with most instruction conducted in Spanish using comprehensible input.
The class includes a strong cultural component, introducing students to traditions from the Spanish-speaking world.

records.title: Statistics 12
facts: Statistics 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students, developing understanding of tools for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data.
Topics include variation and distribution, probability and uncertainty, and how data influences decision-making and policy.
The course emphasizes critical thinking through analysis of real-world data and project-based learning.
This course is intended for students considering post-secondary programs in STEM or data-driven fields like social sciences, politics, or business.

records.title: String Ensemble
facts: The String Ensemble course is for students with intermediate to advanced proficiency on string instruments.
The ensemble's repertoire includes classical, modern, folk, and popular music.
Guest performances from vocalists, harp, piano, or percussion may occasionally be featured.
The String Ensemble participates in music festivals across British Columbia and at MusicFest Nationals.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Instrumental Music: Orchestra 10, 11, 12.

records.title: Studio Arts Rotation
facts: The Studio Arts Rotation course is designed for Grade 10 students interested in visual arts.
Students rotate through three programs: 3D Pottery, Drawing & Painting, and Graphic Art & Design.
Students spend one term in each program over the course of the year.
This course provides foundational skills for continuing in these subject areas in Grade 11 and 12.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Studio Art 10, 11.

records.title: The Art of Leadership
facts: The Art of Leadership course is available to students in Grades 10-12.
Students in this course learn about leadership and how to create positive change through service to the Brentwood community.
Students develop leadership awareness and apply skills to activities and events that make the Library Learning Commons (LLC) a central point for interaction and learning.
Leadership activities can include initiatives related to student clubs (B-Well, OMNI, BIPOC, Women's Society, SAC, BEAT), student councils (Arts, Academic, Athletic), and House leadership.
Other activities may include reading contests, author visits, and events for special day or month promotions.

records.title: Theatre Company
facts: The Theatre Company course is an advanced class for experienced actors.
Students should have completed the junior course or have prior stage experience.
The course focuses on characterization, role development, and performing scene work from theatre and film.
Students will fine-tune their physical presence through movement and voice.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Theatre Company 11 and 12.

records.title: Theatre Production
facts: The Theatre Production course supports Brentwood's performing arts program.
Students can gain experience in stage management, lighting, sound editing and design, projections, special effects, and theatrical design.
The course also covers event planning, production experience, and front-of-house and box office management.
Theatre Production provides technical support for live productions in the George Killy Theatre and across campus.
This course is open to Grades 10, 11, and 12, and Grade 9 with instructor permission.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Theatre Production 10, 11, 12.

records.title: Urban & Sustainability Studies 12
facts: Urban & Sustainability Studies 12 is an elective course for Grade 11 and Grade 12 students, exploring the relationship between urbanization, society, and sustainability.
Students examine how urban spaces are shaped by geographic, economic, political, and social forces.
The course focuses on how urban planning decisions can create sustainable futures, using local, national, and international examples.
Students analyze the impact of government policies, urban planning, and innovative sustainability approaches through project-based learning.

records.title: Vocal Ensemble
facts: The Vocal Ensemble explores various genres and styles of singing for mixed voices.
Students learn ensemble musicianship and vocal technique, both with accompaniment and a cappella.
Participants have opportunities to perform in school concerts and at festivals.
Sight-reading experience is not required to join the program.

records.title: Wind Ensemble
facts: The Wind Ensemble course is for instrumental musicians with intermediate to advanced performance ability.
The ensemble includes woodwinds, brass, and percussion instruments.
The repertoire is diverse, covering orchestral transcriptions, traditional concert band pieces, world music, pop, rock, jazz, and show tunes.
The Wind Ensemble participates in on-campus and off-campus events, including local music festivals, provincial competitions, and Nationals.
Ministry Credit is awarded for Instrumental Music: Concert Band 10, 11, 12.

records.title: Woodworking
facts: Woodworking is a hands-on course focused on skill-building in woodworking, furniture making, and craftsmanship.
The course emphasizes safe and effective use of hand tools, power tools, and woodworking machinery.
Students learn various techniques including measuring, joinery, sanding, finishing, and project assembly.
Students design and construct functional and decorative wooden projects.
The woodworking shop includes equipment such as a table saw, lathe, planer, jointer, bandsaw, drill press, and belt sander.
Safety training in shop procedures and tool handling is a core component of the program.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Woodwork 10, 11, and 12.

records.title: Yearbook
facts: The Yearbook course is for students interested in documenting the school year through pictures and print.
Students photograph academics, athletics, fine arts, and other school activities.
Students must be able to work independently and meet deadlines.
Experience with an SLR digital camera is beneficial.
This course awards Ministry Credit for Graphic Production 11 and 12.

records.title: Academic Classrooms
facts: Classrooms in five buildings feature digital projection, audio, and movable furniture for flexible learning environments.

records.title: Anthony C. Carr Boathouse
facts: The Anthony C. Carr Boathouse opened in the fall of 2024.
It is a leading-edge facility located on the Brentwood campus waterfront.
Rowers train in the waters surrounding Mill Bay.

records.title: Arts Gallery
facts: Brentwood displays student artwork in its hallways and galleries.
Categories of art showcased include 2D Art, Pottery, Dance, 3D Art, and Photography.

records.title: Athletic Facilities
facts: Athletic facilities include a climbing wall, rowing shells, kayaks, an ice rink, basketball courts, and tennis courts.

records.title: Athletic Facilities & Support
facts: The school provides world-class athletic facilities, specialized coaches for Strength & Conditioning, and full-time certified athletic therapists for injury support and rehabilitation.
A sport rehabilitation program, including an anti-gravity treadmill, aids safe return to sport.
External activities like equestrian or mountain biking can be arranged during non-programmed times, but families are responsible for logistics and these do not count for PE credit.

records.title: Brentwood Library Resources
facts: The library provides access to articles, books, journals, and various databases for research and learning.

records.title: Brentwood Robotics Lab
facts: The robotics program is conducted in the fully equipped Brentwood Robotics Lab.

records.title: Briggs Health, Wellness & Athletic Therapy Centre
facts: The 2,000 sq.ft. Briggs Health, Wellness & Athletic Therapy Centre offers injury prevention and recovery support.
Full-time athletic therapists guide students using recovery equipment, including an anti-gravity treadmill.

records.title: Campus Art Gallery
facts: The main corridor of the Centre for Arts and Humanities hosts the largest campus art gallery.
Student work from various arts programs is displayed on multi-tiered walls.
Art pieces are also curated and accessible in other campus buildings, including the Kyrsa Collection of Brentonian Art.

records.title: Campus Overview
facts: Brentwood's 90-acre oceanfront campus on Vancouver Island features over 1 km of waterfront with views of the Gulf Islands and Mount Baker. Buildings are close, fostering community.

records.title: Centre for Arts and Humanities
facts: Facilities include drawing and painting studios, a pottery studio with 20 wheels and three kilns, photography darkrooms and digital equipment, woodworking and sculpture workshops, and a robotics lab.

records.title: Centre for Innovation and Learning
facts: The 72,000 sq.ft. oceanfront Centre for Innovation and Learning includes a new boathouse for rowing.
Academic features are Learning Neighbourhoods, a Science Superlab, Collaborative Atrium Space, and Waterfront Learning Spaces.

records.title: Cisco Phone System
facts: The Cisco Phone system provides local phones on the Brentwood campus.
It offers features such as local calling, external calling, voicemail, and call forwarding.
Extensions are either tied to individuals or are generic for locations or multiple handsets.

records.title: Climbing Wall
facts: A 50-foot climbing wall is located in the Athletic Centre.

records.title: Crooks Hall student services
facts: Crooks Hall contains dining, McNeill’s Student Centre, Hospitality Services and the School Store.

records.title: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre
facts: This centre is home to the basketball program.
The Wheaton Gym within the centre has space for two full-sized basketball courts.
The facility includes four change rooms and four digital scoreboards.
The Strength & Conditioning Centre is available for players to further their athletic abilities.

records.title: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre
facts: The 60,000 sq.ft. Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre features the 21,000 sq.ft. Wheaton Gym (double gymnasium), four change rooms, a livestream media booth, and multipurpose rooms.

It also includes a 7,500 sq.ft. Strength & Conditioning Centre, Hardy Cardio Room, a 50 ft. high Climbing & Bouldering Wall, three squash courts, and the Foote Field House with a viewing deck and kitchen facilities.

records.title: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre
facts: Student-athletes are supported by facilities in and around the Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre.
Facilities include four grass fields, a turf practice field, and change rooms off Gillespie Field.
Players can use the Strength & Conditioning Centre for sport-specific training.

records.title: Environmental Sustainability Initiatives
facts: Brentwood educates on sustainable living and environmental stewardship, offering courses like Environmental Advocacy and Science.
The student-led BEAT group promotes upcycling, clothing exchanges, energy reduction, and leads clean-ups and wetland restoration.
The school has been energy-sensitive since the 1980s, using innovative heating and building controls.
Initiatives include campus-wide recycling, composting, Green Seal products, energy-efficient lighting, and low-flow plumbing.
Brentwood is a registered ecoActive school through PITCH-IN Canada.
The T.
Gil Bunch Centre and Centre for Innovation and Learning use Canada's first ocean-source geo-exchange system.
This geo-exchange system, Vancouver Island's largest, supports four major campus buildings.

records.title: Film & Broadcast Facilities
keywords: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre
facts: Students have access to a 960 sq. ft. sound stage equipped with studio lights and a green screen.
Available equipment includes cinema cameras, lights, audio equipment, and professional editing software.
Live broadcasts are produced from the media booth located in the Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre.
The media booth serves as a central hub for remote cameras and audio feeds from across the campus.

records.title: Foote Athletic Centre
facts: The Foote Athletic Centre gymnasium features four full-sized volleyball courts with extensive surrounding space.
The facility includes four change rooms, a Strength & Conditioning Centre, and the Hardy Cardio Room.
It is also equipped with a livestream media booth.

records.title: Innovations Office Location
facts: The Innovations Office is located on the lower floor of the Centre for Innovation and Learning Building, around the corner from the Science Lab.
