records.title: LLC Hours
facts: The LLC is generally open from 7am to 10pm, Sunday to Saturday.
Evening prep in the LLC is available by signup from 7:30pm to 9:30pm, Monday to Friday.
Ms. Handley's hours are 7:45am to 1:15pm, Monday to Friday.
Mr. Stevens' hours are 8:00am to 4:00pm on M/W/F, 8:00am to 1:15pm T/Th, and 10:00am to 1:15pm Sa.

records.title: Learning Commons and Study Areas
facts: The Learning Commons is a modern library for collaborative or individual study, supported by academic teachers.
During "Prep" (evening study), students can receive extra help.
Other campus study spots include McNeill's Cafe and common areas.

records.title: Library Learning Commons (LLC) Overview
facts: The Library Learning Commons (LLC) is a central hub for students, staff, and the school community, offering resources, support, and collaborative spaces.

records.title: Maeda Health Centre
facts: The Maeda Health Centre provides mental and physical wellness care. The Nursing Team arranges appointments, dispenses medication, and administers immunizations. Medical staff assist students and communicate with House Staff.

records.title: Music Facilities
facts: Music facilities include the T. Gil Bunch Centre for Performing Arts, which houses the 431-seat George Killy Theatre with professional sound and lighting.
Rehearsal spaces like the Asper Music Room and an oceanfront amphitheatre are also available.

records.title: Musical Facilities
facts: The T. Gil Bunch Centre for Performing Arts houses the musical program, featuring a 20,000 sq. ft. facility.
It includes a 431-seat George Killy Theatre with a sprung floor, orchestra pit, and advanced sound and lighting systems, along with a dance studio, green room, four dressing rooms, and a music suite.

records.title: Oceanfront Athletic Facilities
facts: Oceanfront facilities are used for rowing, kayaking, canoeing, and open water SCUBA diving.
The annual Brentwood International Regatta hosts rowing crews.

records.title: Oceanfront Campus
facts: The campus features 1 kilometer of coastline.
It offers oceanfront activities and outdoor classes.

records.title: Outdoor Recreation Areas
facts: Students can ski and snowboard on nearby Mount Washington.
Local forest trails are available for hiking and running.

records.title: Photography Facilities & Equipment
facts: Photography facilities include a professional darkroom and a 960 sq. ft. photo studio equipped with multiple backdrops and studio lights.
Digital Photography students have access to inkjet printers and dedicated photo-quality monitors.

records.title: Playing Fields & Tennis Courts
facts: Brentwood has four grass sports fields, one turf field, and eight tennis courts for training and competition.

records.title: Pottery Studio
facts: The pottery studio is 2,000 sq. ft. and equipped with 20 potting wheels, storage space, drying racks, and three kilns.
Students have access to all necessary tools and equipment for projects from raw clay to presentation.
Dedicated space is available for students to display their work in the pottery studio gallery and the main Centre for Arts and Humanities campus gallery.

records.title: Science Superlab
facts: This shared, open lab space for all sciences is based on a post-secondary model.
It integrates biology, chemistry, and physics concepts with collaborative equipment, and has adjoining classrooms.

records.title: Strength & Conditioning Centre
facts: Rugby players follow a comprehensive Strength & Conditioning program.
The Strength & Conditioning Centre and Hardy Cardio Room are equipped with weights and cardio equipment.
Full-time conditioning coaches develop sport-specific training programs.

records.title: Summer Camp Travel and Accommodation
facts: Campers arrange travel to Vancouver Island.
A complimentary shuttle is provided from Victoria International Airport (YYJ) and Swartz Bay ferry terminal.
Overnight campers stay in a Brentwood boarding house with twin XL beds, desks, chairs, towels, bedding, shared kitchens, flatscreens, common areas, and coin-operated laundry.

records.title: Sustainability Initiatives
facts: The campus uses a geothermal loop for heating, building controls for specific heating, and automatic fresh air delivery based on occupancy. Landscape design includes irrigation, bio swells, and 'purple water' plumbing provisions.

records.title: T. Gil Bunch Centre and George Killy Theatre
facts: The Bunch Centre contains the 431-seat George Killy Theatre, dance and music studios, a green room and four dressing rooms. The Asper Room supports band rehearsal and media production.

records.title: Theatre Production Venues
facts: In-house productions are held in the George Killy Theatre.
Students also support performances in Crooks Dining Hall and the open-air Campbell Commons gathering space.

records.title: Visual Arts Studios
facts: The Centre for Arts and Humanities features 3,600 sq. ft. of dedicated visual arts studios.
Two main studios are equipped with easels, sinks, smocks, and ample table space.
An AP Studio offers additional space for advanced students working on 2D pieces, 3D sculpture, and fashion.
Studios are designed with large windows to provide natural light and ocean views.

records.title: Woodworking Shop
facts: The spacious woodworking shop is equipped with professional tools.
Available equipment includes a table saw, lathe, planer, bandsaw, drill press, and drum sander.

records.title: Acceptable & Unacceptable IT Use
facts: Use school IT for educational activities and reasonable personal use.
Prohibited acts include illegal activities, copyright infringement, excessive bandwidth, password sharing, unauthorized access, data manipulation, and creating offensive content.
Report infractions to the Director of IT.

records.title: Accessibility Plan
facts: The Accessible British Columbia Regulation, under the Accessible British Columbia Act, came into force on September 1, 2022.
Schools are required to have an Accessibility Committee, an Accessibility Plan, and a tool for feedback on accessibility by September 1, 2023.
The goal of the act is to improve opportunities for people with disabilities and involve them in identifying, removing, and preventing barriers.
The ISABC has developed a barrier reporting form for community members to provide feedback on accessible experiences, with options for anonymous responses.
Questions, comments, or feedback regarding the collective ISABC Accessibility Plan can be directed to Bonnie Fisher at bonniefisher@isabc.ca.

records.title: Confidentiality and Data Usage for BRAIN Study
facts: Participation is voluntary; student identity is protected.
Participants get a unique scan ID, unlinked to their name.
Scan results or personal info are not shared without explicit consent.
All collected data remains anonymous and confidential.

records.title: Course Change Policy
facts: Course changes can be made via the Course Registration Form until spring break.
After spring break, changes require University Counselling.

records.title: External Links and Liability
facts: Brentwood websites may link to external sites, but the school is not responsible for their content or policies.
Brentwood accepts no liability for website information, impaired access, or damages from use.
Users acknowledge the school is not liable for defamatory, offensive, or illegal conduct by any user.

records.title: Health Forms and Policies
facts: Health-related documents include the Brentwood Student Physical Health Form and the Concussion Policy and Return to Learn & Play Protocol.

records.title: IT Acceptable Use Policy Scope
facts: This policy outlines responsible use of school technology for safety, security, and reliability.
It applies to all users, school-owned IT, and students' personal devices while in school care.

records.title: Indigenous-Focused Graduation Requirement (IFGR)
facts: The BC Ministry of Education mandates an Indigenous-Focused Graduation Requirement.
Students can fulfill this in Grade 10 with English First Peoples 10, or in Grades 11/12 with Contemporary Indigenous Studies 12 (also a senior Social Studies credit) or English First Peoples 12.

records.title: Information Handling and Rights
facts: Personal information is collected for educational services.
Consent is generally required for collection, use, or disclosure, and can be withdrawn with written notice.
Information may be disclosed with consent or as legally required (e.g., to other institutions, service providers).
Data is protected by security safeguards, with access restricted to authorized employees and secured files.
Individuals can request corrections and access their records.
Data is retained only as long as necessary for its purpose or legal requirements.

records.title: Information Technology Acceptable Use Policy
facts: The Information Technology Acceptable Use Policy outlines how the School’s technology services and resources are to be used responsibly and respectfully.
This policy is available for review in the Student Handbook.

records.title: Privacy Policy Overview and Officer
facts: Brentwood College School safeguards personal information of parents, students, employees, and volunteers, adhering to British Columbia's PIPA standards.
The policy details collection, use, and disclosure of personal information.
David Burton is the Privacy Officer, accountable for compliance, and can be contacted at privacyofficer@brentwood.bc.ca.

records.title: Private Music Lesson Registration and Fees
facts: A signed registration form is required.
Programs run September-June; fees are pro-rated for late enrollment.
The first three lessons are a probationary period for withdrawal/dismissal with a refund (minus probationary fee).
After probation, students are enrolled for the full year with no refunds for withdrawal.
Tuition is billed separately.

records.title: Required Forms and Handbook
facts: All students and parents must complete Informed Consent, Health (via BlueHealth), and a Food Services Questionnaire in MySchool.
Private Music Lessons are an optional form.
Parents/guardians must review the Student Handbook for the upcoming year before completing Informed Consent.

records.title: Required Travel Documents by Citizenship
facts: Canadian citizens need a valid Canadian passport.
Permanent Residents require a valid passport, a Canadian Permanent Resident card, and a Multiple Entry US Visitor's Visa.
USA students need a valid USA passport, a Multiple Entry Canadian Visa, and a Study Permit.
International students (non-USA) require a valid passport, a Multiple Entry Canadian Visa, a Multiple Entry US Visitor's Visa or ESTA, and a Study Permit.

records.title: School Access to Data & Privacy
facts: The school may access all information on its IT systems for administration, audits, investigations, or legal compliance.
Users should not expect privacy for personal use of school resources.

records.title: School Policies and Handbook
facts: Key documents include the Informed Consent Guide, Student Handbook, Principles of Community, Academic InteGRITy Policy, and Learning Resources Policy.

records.title: Student Leadership Application Process 2026/27
facts: Applications for 2026/27 leadership roles are due by 5:00 pm on May 13, 2026, via the Student Leadership Form.
Grade 11 students applying for Head or Assistant Head Prefect must submit a cover letter, resume, 100-word summary, and Houseparent support email to lorraine.keen@brentwood.ca.
On May 25, 2026, students (grades 9-12) and faculty will be polled for these roles; only Grade 11s for Grad President.
The Head of School makes final appointments based on faculty recommendations.
Results will be announced on June 12, 2026, at Closing Ceremonies.

records.title: Student Penalties for Misuse
facts: Penalties for students include warnings, loss of privileges, material removal, suspension, expulsion, charges for costs, or legal action.

records.title: Study Permits
facts: Families must apply for and renew study permits via the Canadian Embassy or Consulate; Brentwood provides supporting documents.
A study permit is mandatory for all students who do not have a Canadian passport or are not Permanent Residents, regardless of stay length.
Online application is recommended for faster processing.

records.title: Terms of Service and Website Use
facts: Use of Brentwood College School websites is subject to its Privacy Policy and Terms of Use.
Users agree to these terms, which may be modified.
Violations can lead to denied access to password-protected areas.

records.title: Travel Document Responsibility
facts: Parents are responsible for identifying and securing all official documents required for their child's attendance and travel during the school year.
Students traveling with school groups within Canada or to the USA need specific identification.
Contact the nearest Canadian Consulate or Embassy for assistance with document requirements.

records.title: Website Data and User Accounts
facts: The web server collects domain names and IP addresses for statistics, but not personal email addresses.
Cookies are used for anonymous information, but do not reveal personally identifiable data not otherwise disclosed.
Brentwood does not sell or rent identifiable information.
Users are responsible for account and password confidentiality for protected areas.
School logos and graphics are trademarks; unauthorized use is prohibited.

records.title: 2D Art Program
facts: The 2D Art Program helps students develop creative expression skills at all skill levels.
Courses are available for both beginners and advanced students.
Instructors for the program include Angela Andersen and Ivana Cappelletto.

records.title: Annual Rowing Regatta Schedule
facts: Includes Green Lake Training Camp (Oct), Head and Tail of the Gorge (Oct), Head of the Charles (Oct), Frostbite Regatta (Nov), Head of the Lake (Nov), Kraken Erg (Feb), Elk Lake Spring Regatta (Mar), Spring Break Training Camp (Mar), Maple Bay Regatta (Apr), Brentwood International Regatta (Apr), Windermere Cup Regatta (May), Shawnigan Lake Regatta (May), CSSRA Camp (May), Nanaimo Sprints (May), and CSSRA Regatta (June).

records.title: Arts Day Rowing Program
facts: Open to Grades 9-12, practices Mon/Wed/Fri, 3-5 PM.
No experience needed; Learn-to-Row offered through October.

records.title: Arts Program
facts: Over 30 year-long arts courses are available, allowing students to select up to four.
Professional instructors use dedicated facilities for arts programs.
Arts blocks occur on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons.

records.title: Arts on Campus
facts: Visual artists (painters, photographers, 3D Art/Sculpture) use the campus for inspiration. Photojournalism students cover campus events. Musicians utilize the amphitheatre on sunny days.

records.title: Arts, Athletics, Trips, and Outings
facts: The school hosts arts performances (musicals, concerts, drama, art shows) and competitive athletics showcase games.
Annual trips include academic, arts, athletics, and a biennial service trip.
Winter sports opportunities feature weekly ski/snowboard excursions to Mt. Washington and a full-school ski day.
Off-campus house outings visit local areas like Victoria, shopping malls, and skating rinks.

records.title: Athlete Participation in BRAIN Club Research
facts: Brentwood students enrolled in basketball, field hockey, ice hockey, rowing, soccer, rugby, or Jiu-Jitsu may be eligible to participate in the BRAIN club's athlete research.

records.title: Athletics Program
facts: Athletics are scheduled on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday afternoons.
Students choose a different sport each term from recreational and competitive options.

records.title: Athletics Program & Options
facts: Brentwood's athletics program offers over 20 recreational and competitive sports, with students selecting a new one each term.

Options include Basketball, Climbing, Cross Country Running, Dance, Field Hockey, Fitness Performance, Golf, Ice Hockey, Jiu-Jitsu, Outdoor Pursuits, Rowing, Rugby, Open Water SCUBA, Soccer, Squash, Swimming & Lifesaving, Tennis, Volleyball, and Yoga.
Participation in Brentwood athletics is expected.

records.title: B-Well Program
facts: B-Well is for Grade 11 and 12 students with voluntary peer-support training. Members develop mental wellness literacy and organize events like the Wellness Conference, peer counselling, and health awareness campaigns.

records.title: BRAIN (Brentwood Research Action & Innovation in Neuroscience) Club
facts: The BRAIN club at Brentwood College School involves high school students in neuroscience research.
Students in the BRAIN club collaborated with researchers from institutions like Simon Fraser University, Mayo Clinic, and Columbia University.
The club contributed to a study on subconcussive impacts in high school sports, which was published in Scientific Reports.
The study used portable brain-scanning technology (NeuroCatch® Platform) to measure cognitive brain function in athletes.
The research found that athletes in high-contact sports had delayed cognitive and auditory responses, with female athletes showing larger disruptions in attention and cognitive processing.
The BRAIN club continues its research, exploring brain recovery during summer break, the effects of different sports, and potential treatment options.
Science Technician Lily Stewart currently sponsors the BRAIN club.

records.title: BRAIN Club (Brentwood Research, Action, & Innovation in Neuroscience)
facts: BRAIN is a club for Brentwood students and alumni to involve high school students in neuroscience studies.
Students contribute to research alongside global leaders.
The club is studying if repeated head impacts in high school athletes affect cognitive ability.

records.title: Basketball Program
facts: The program offers competition for boys and girls through league play and tournaments.
Students new to basketball can learn in the fall and spring terms.
Committed competitive players can participate year-round.
The program emphasizes skill development, commitment to teammates, and a love of the game.
The Senior Boys’ team won Silver at Provincials in 2024.
The Senior Girls’ Team won Silver at Islands in 2024 and qualified for Provincials twice in the past three years.
Several students have gone on to play basketball at post-secondary schools.

records.title: Brentwood Chess Club
facts: The Brentwood Chess Club is listed among the library's resources.

records.title: Brentwood Musical Production
facts: The Brentwood Musical is a performance program for actors, singers, and dancers, culminating in a full-length "triple-threat" production each spring.
It involves over 70 students and crew, supported by a live orchestra, and runs for a week in the George Killy Theatre.
Students participate both on stage and in technical roles.

records.title: Brentwood Summer Day Camps 2027
facts: Brentwood College School offers day camps for ages 7-17, weekdays in July, including snacks and lunch.
Registration for 2027 opens December 2026.
Rock Climbing Camp (ages 8-14) runs July 5-9 and July 12-16, 9:00 am-4:00 pm, with certified instructors.
Theatre Camp has a Junior program (ages 7-10) July 4-9 and a Senior program (ages 11-16) July 11-16.
Theatre camps run Sunday 12:00 pm-5:00 pm and Monday-Friday 9:00 am-4:00 pm, led by industry professionals, culminating in a presentation.

records.title: Brentwood Summer Overnight Camps 2027
facts: Brentwood College School offers new overnight summer camps for ages 13-17 in 2027.
Campers live in a boarding house with meals, excursions, and evening activities.
Registration opens December 2026.
Marine Sciences Camp (ages 13-17) runs two weeks: Coastal Systems & Marine Life (June 27-July 3) and Boats, Whales & Whole Ecosystems (July 4-10).

records.title: Climbing Program
facts: The program is offered in all three terms.
It teaches the basics of top-rope, lead climbing, and bouldering.
Students utilize the on-campus climbing wall, nearby gyms, and popular west coast outdoor locations.
Local and Sport Climbing British Columbia competitions are included.
All skill levels are welcomed.

records.title: Competitive Dance Company
facts: The Dance Company is a competitive dance program open to students of all levels.
The program offers opportunities to perform and compete at three competitive events in Vancouver and Vancouver Island.
Students can pursue dance examinations (RAD, ADAPT) or higher-level competitions (YAGP, Nuvo) through this program.
The Dance Company rehearses outside of regular class time.
Three guest choreographers visit each year to provide diverse choreography and dance experiences.
The program covers all styles of dance, including solos, duos, trios, small groups, and large groups.

records.title: Course Selection Process 2026-27
facts: Course selection for 2026-27 requires reviewing grade requirements and course descriptions.
Students select academic courses first, then arts, then fall athletics.
New students get a 'New Student Account and Course Selection' email after enrollment.
Returning Grades 9-10 students don't need University Counselling review for academic courses.
Returning Grades 11-12 students review academic courses with University Counsellors.

records.title: Cross Country Running Program
facts: The program emphasizes inclusivity and nurturing excellent wellness habits.
Weekly destination runs explore parts of Vancouver Island, including Goldstream Park, Mount Tzouhalem, Thetis Lake, Elk Lake, and Gowlland Tod Provincial Park.
Cross-training activities include spinning, aqua aerobics, and boxing.
Opportunities for serious runners include both road and trail races.
In the fall term, Brentwood competes in the Cowichan Valley Running Series and regional meets to qualify for provincial championships.
Both boys’ and girls’ teams went to the provincial meet in 2022.
Runners from the program have competed at the post-secondary and NCAA Division 1 levels.

records.title: Dance Program
facts: The Brentwood Dance Program offers various challenge levels and styles.
Megan Rea is a dance instructor with professional performing and competing experience.
The program includes Dance: Advanced, Dance: Beginner, Dance: Intermediate, and Sport Dance.
Facilities are located in the T. Gil Bunch Centre for the Performing Arts.
The dedicated dance studio features a sprung floor, full-length mirrors, ballet barres, and built-in sound and video systems.
Performances take place in the 431-seat George Killy Theatre, which has a sprung floor, orchestra pit, and advanced sound, communications, video, and stage lighting systems.

records.title: Debate & Model United Nations Program
facts: The Debate and Model UN program attracts over 80 students annually, developing communication and oratory skills.
Students can explore debate as a standalone activity and public speaking combined with Model United Nations experience.
Teachers introduce students of all skill levels to research-based arguments and mock trials.
Students have opportunities to participate in class debates and attend debate competitions against other schools.
Model UN enhances formal communication skills and allows participation in conferences to negotiate contemporary and historical issues.
Top debaters and speakers may travel to provincial and national conferences and competitions each year.
Instructors for the program include Sara Checkley and Michelle Legassicke.

records.title: Experiential Learning and Environment
facts: Classes use the mild climate for outdoor learning. Students observe salmon in Mill Bay estuary and Shawnigan Creek in fall; the environmental club aids salmon transfer. Science classes study marine biology in Mill Bay.

records.title: Field Hockey Program
facts: Field Hockey is primarily a girls' competitive program in the fall term, with a co-ed option in spring.
The coaching staff fields three teams in the fall: First XI, Second XI, and Development Team for new players.
Tournament opportunities include the Ferreira Cup, Friendship Cup, BC Independent Schools Association Championship, BC Secondary Provincial Championships, and Development Tournament.
In 2024/25, the girls' team placed 9th in the BC Secondary event.
Training occurs at the on-campus turf field and the nearby Cowichan Sportsplex.

records.title: Film & Broadcast Program
facts: The film and video programs offer opportunities for students of all skill levels to pursue screen arts.
Course offerings cover various video production styles, including short film and live broadcast.
The Filmmaking Program builds teams of content creators to produce movies or web series.
Justine Backlund is an instructor for the program.

records.title: Fitness Performance Program
facts: The Fitness Performance program is open to students of all skill levels and aims to enhance cardio, core strength, and flexibility.
Offered in all three terms, it can complement team sports by developing healthy fitness habits.
Activities include running local mountains, kick-boxing, cardio and strength circuits, swimming, cycling, hot yoga, and tabata training.
Workouts are designed with participants' needs and goals in mind.
Training takes place across campus, including outdoors and indoors at the Strength & Conditioning Centre.

records.title: Golf Program
facts: The Golf Program is offered during the spring term.
It welcomes students of all skill levels, from beginners to junior national team players.
Practices occur three times per week during sport afternoons at the Cowichan Golf Club.
Players work with club professionals on the driving range, putting greens, and on the course.
Competitive players participate in tournaments at local courses like Arbutus Ridge Golf Club and Victoria Golf Club.
Students can attend competitive events such as ISAs, Victoria Police Golf Tournament, Islands, and BC Secondary Provincial Championships.
The season concludes with The John Garvey Cup, a student versus staff event, and The Soukop Championship, a school-hosted tournament for top male and female golfers.

records.title: Grade 8 Day Program Course Selection
facts: The Grade 8 Day Program has a specific curriculum.
Grade 8 students may join senior school arts and athletics based on space, addressed during September's Orientation Week.

records.title: Grade 8 Extra-Curricular Activities
facts: Participation in Brentwood's arts and athletics programs is not mandatory for Grade 8 students, but interested students are welcome to join.
Arts programs run on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons for the full school year.
Athletics programs take place on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday afternoons, with different sports available each term.
Competitive teams may practice or compete more than three days per week.

records.title: Grade 8 Program
facts: The Brentwood Grade 8 Program has its own independent timetable, purpose, and goals.
It prepares students for the Grade 9-12 post-secondary preparatory program and supports executive functioning development.
The program primarily caters to day students with a five-day schedule, aiding transition to the six-day Tripartite Program.
Brentwood's facilities and some programs are accessible to Grade 8 students.

records.title: Grade 8 Program
facts: The Grade 8 program has an independent timetable, preparing students for Grade 9-12. Mandatory arts (Mon, Wed, Fri) and athletics (Tue, Thu, Sat) programs allow students to choose different sports each term.

records.title: Grade 8 Rowing Program
facts: Independent of the Grade 9-12 program.
Grade 8 students try rowing on water in Sept/Oct and May/June, and on machines in Jan/Feb during PE blocks.
Aims for a safe, positive introduction.

records.title: Ice Hockey Program
facts: The Ice Hockey program starts in the fall term at the local Kerry Park Arena.
It focuses on fundamental skill development, including skating, puck-handling, passing, shooting, and checking.
The program accommodates all skill levels, from beginners to experienced players.
Beginners play with the Development Team, while more experienced players compete in league play on the Brentwood Senior Team.
The Senior Team participates in tournaments under BC Hockey (Hockey Canada) oversight, including travel outside of BC.
The girls' program plays games against local women's teams, high school teams, and teams in Vancouver.
The season culminates with the annual Ross Cup tournament in the third week of February.
In 2023/24, the Senior team won Silver at the Ross Cup event.

records.title: Jiu-Jitsu Program
facts: The Jiu-Jitsu Program is guided by principles of honour, integrity, and empathy.
Students of all skill levels learn efficiency, patience, control, and mindfulness.
Students have the opportunity to participate in all three terms and compete both locally and provincially.
Jiu-Jitsu is known as the “gentle art” because it involves no striking and allows a smaller person to use leverage for self-defense.
Grappling and ground fighting are the primary vehicles for technique development.
Each student is provided a numbered gi (martial arts uniform) to use throughout the term.

records.title: Media Arts Program
facts: The Media Arts Program offers students options in artistic traditions, team settings, and tools.
It focuses on developing transferable skills in digital communication, graphic design, yearbook, and photojournalism.

records.title: Metamorphosis 9
facts: Metamorphosis 9 is an innovative Grade 9 program.
This integrated program combines Science 9, Social Studies 9, and Applied Design, Skills and Technology 9.
The course includes mini-lectures, labs, assignments, project-based activities, simulations, design challenges, and field trips.
Students work in various settings and are exposed to diverse learning methodologies.
Community involvement, including field trips across the island, is part of the program.
Students learn to manage and improve their executive functioning skills.

records.title: Multisport Program
facts: The Multisport program is offered during the spring term.
It focuses on friendly competition across a wide range of activities without the pressure of winning medals.
Students can enjoy athletics across many campus venues, including the gym, turf fields, and grass fields.
The program emphasizes effort and attitude, promoting inclusivity for all skill levels.
It provides opportunities for students to try new sports and develop excellent fitness habits.

records.title: Music Program
facts: The Music Program is integral to performing arts at the school, supporting cultural events and competitive opportunities.
It offers informal performance chances for students, including an annual all-student talent showcase.

records.title: Open Water SCUBA Diving Program
facts: The program supports novice and advanced SCUBA divers.
Most students complete their PADI Open Water Diver Certification.
Some students complete their Advanced Open Water Certification.
Training begins with indoor pool visits and in-class sessions.
The program includes open water ocean dives off campus docks and nearby beaches.
Boat dives are also offered.
The program encourages wonderment, exploration, and conservation.

records.title: Outdoor Learning Opportunities
facts: The oceanfront campus and mild climate are utilized for outdoor lessons, such as calculus in the amphitheatre or biological analysis of the Saanich Inlet ecosystem.

records.title: Outdoor Pursuits Program
facts: The Outdoor Pursuits (ODP) program teaches students about environmental stewardship.
The fall term includes kayak safety, paddling techniques, equipment care, and multi-day camping trips, such as circumnavigating Salt Spring Island.
Experienced Grade 11 and 12 students can become student leaders in the winter term.
The spring term focuses on whitewater kayaking, culminating in a regional event on the Cowichan River.

records.title: Participation in BRAIN Concussion Study
facts: Participants are assigned to contact or non-contact sports groups.
Each group undergoes a 10-20 minute non-invasive Neurocatch scan at term start and end.
Volunteer hours are given to student scanners.
Eligibility: 15-17 years old at fall term start, parental consent, no auditory issues, no concussion in prior 6 weeks.
Eligible sports include Basketball, Field Hockey, Ice Hockey, Rowing, Soccer, Rugby, and Jiu-Jitsu.

records.title: Photography Program
facts: The Photography Program explores both traditional and digital workflows, catering to all skill levels.
Projects focus on developing composition and technique, with opportunities for students to showcase their work at public art shows.

records.title: Robotics Program
facts: Students learn to construct and program both actively-controlled and autonomous robots using VEX Robotics technology.
Students can join the robotics team to compete in regional, provincial, and international competitions.
Instructors for robotics are Julie Carere, Scott Doehler, and Jeff Szeryk.

records.title: Rowing Program
facts: The rowing program welcomes athletes of all skill levels.
It is led by four-time Olympian David Calder, an Old Brentonian.
Training occurs throughout the year, with the competitive season in the spring term.
Crews travel to regional and national regattas, including the Canadian Secondary Schools Rowing Association Championships (CSSRAs).
Top members may attend prestigious events like the Head of the Charles, Windermere Cup, and Royal English Henley.
Brentwood hosts the annual Brentwood International Regatta.
In 2024, Brentwood crews earned 5 Gold Medals at the CSSRAs.
The program can be taken during arts afternoons.

records.title: Rugby Program
facts: The rugby program is inclusive and welcomes students of all skill levels.
Students train throughout the year, with the competitive season in the spring.
Both boys' and girls' squads regularly qualify for provincial championships in May.
In 2024, the 1st XV Boys won Gold at Islands and placed 4th at Provincials.
Brentwood also competes in Rugby 7s.

records.title: Saturday Activities
facts: Saturday nights feature major school events, including athletics showcases and arts performances.
Each boarding house hosts an 'open house' evening annually.
Houseparents also organize relaxed activities for students in their houses on Saturday evenings.

records.title: School-wide Leadership Positions 2026/27
facts: For 2026/27, leadership positions include Head Prefect, Assistant Head Prefects (Academics, Arts, Athletics), and House Captains for Alex, Allard, Ellis, Hope, Mackenzie, Privett, Rogers, and Whittall Houses.

Additional roles are Captains for Student Activities Committee (SAC), B-Well, Brentwood Environmental Action Team (BEAT), Open-Minded Non-discriminatory Individuals (OMNI), Grad President, and Black, Indigenous, People of Colour (BIPOC).

records.title: Skiing & Snowboarding Program
facts: Brentwood offers weekly Sunday ski trips to Mt. Washington Alpine Resort during the ski season, typically eight trips in the second term.
Sunday trips include options for downhill skiing, snowboarding, cross-country skiing, or tubing, with lessons and equipment rentals available.
A full-school ski day is held on a Wednesday in late January or early February at Mt. Washington Alpine Resort, which is optional for students.
An optional Winter Mid-Term Trip is available for international students who cannot travel home, visiting a ski resort in the BC Interior.
The Winter Mid-Term Trip includes over five full days of skiing or snowboarding, and opportunities for ice skating, tubing, snowshoeing, cross-country skiing, and evening activities.

records.title: Soccer Program
facts: The soccer program is inclusive, with boys competing in the fall and girls in the spring.
Skills development occurs through the winter.
Junior players with aptitude may practice with older players.
Teams compete at junior and senior levels.
Teams participate in university-hosted tournaments and the BC Independent Schools Association Championship Tournament (ISAs).
In 2024/25, the Senior Boys Soccer team won the Bronze Medal at the Provincial Championship.
The mild climate allows for year-round outdoor training.

records.title: Social Events, House Life, and SAC
facts: Social events include formal dinners, dances (e.g., Snowball, Spring Formal), and culturally themed meals.
Boarding houses host annual open houses and in-house activities like pancake breakfasts, movie/game nights, and communal cooking.
The Student Activities Committee (SAC) organizes numerous events throughout the year.
The weekly Sunday Brunch is a community highlight, featuring seasonal themes and diverse menus.

records.title: Sport Dance Program
facts: The Sport Dance Program is open to students of all ages and skill levels.
It aims to promote a lifelong love of dance and physical activity.
The program is available in all three terms, with competitive and non-competitive options.
Students learn ballet, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, tap, and participate in strength and flexibility classes.
Opportunities include competing at local events, taking auditions, preparing for dance examinations, and working with dance professionals.
All dance students can perform at the annual Evening of Dance showcase and take trips to watch professional dancers.

records.title: Sport Dance Program
facts: The Sport Dance Program is open to students of all ages and skill levels.
The program aims to promote a lifelong love of dance and physical activity.
It is available in all three terms, with options for competitive or non-competitive dance.
Students will learn ballet, jazz, contemporary, hip-hop, and tap, in addition to strength and flexibility classes.
Dancers have opportunities to compete at local events, take auditions, prepare for dance examinations, and work with dance professionals.
All dance students can perform at Brentwood's annual showcase, the Evening of Dance.
The program also includes trips to watch professional dancers perform.

records.title: Sports Day Rowing Program
facts: Offers supplemental training and racing for selected experienced rowers on Tue/Thu/Sat, including morning sessions.
Grades 9-10 Arts Day rowers must do a second competitive sport on Sports Days in Terms 1 & 2, unless U17 competing nationally.

records.title: Squash Program
keywords: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletics Centre
BC Independent Schools Association Championship Squash Tournament
facts: The Squash Program is offered in all three terms at the school.
Students can develop competitive skills or a lifelong recreational skill through the program.
Training sessions include cardio, technical drills, and multiple games.
The program competes in the BC Independent Schools Association Championship Squash Tournament, the Quadra Sports Invitational, and the Jesters Junior Squash Tournament.
The Eldon and Anne Foote Athletics Centre features three squash courts with a viewing area and seating.
Gustavo Verna is a coach for the Squash program.

records.title: Strength & Conditioning Program
keywords: Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre
facts: Strength & Conditioning (S&C) is a voluntary training opportunity.
Students typically participate in S&C during free arts blocks on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday afternoons, in addition to their main sport.
The program utilizes the facilities in the Eldon and Anne Foote Athletic Centre.
S&C coaches aim to educate students on the benefits of training for confidence, injury prevention, and peak performance.
The program teaches safe techniques first, then advances students based on their skill level and goals.
Programs are available for all levels, from novice to elite athletes.
Sport-specific programming is considered based on individual and team goals.
Tanya Scheck and Shane Thompson are coaches for Strength & Conditioning.

records.title: Student Activities
facts: The Student Activities Committee (SAC) and staff organize a vibrant calendar of events.
Activities include spirit weeks, athletics, arts performances, dinners, dances, Interhouse Competitions, Off Campus Outings, and Winter Ski Trips.

records.title: Student Activities and Interhouse Competition
facts: Brentwood College School offers diverse social activities to strengthen community and provide enriching experiences.
Students participate in Interhouse Competitions, earning house points and fostering cooperation, collaboration, and sportsmanship.

records.title: Student Leadership
facts: Leadership at Brentwood focuses on service to the community.
Grade 12 students decide how they will lead the school.

records.title: Student Leadership Programs
facts: Brentwood offers various leadership opportunities for students, including roles within houses and project-based class roles.
The Student Executive Council (SEC) includes the Head Prefect, Assistant Head Prefects, House Captains, and leaders for specific groups.

Key student-led groups include the Student Activities Committee (SAC) for social and fundraising events, B-Well for peer wellness support, OMNI for LGBTQIA2S+ community support and discussions, BEAT for environmental action, Grad Council for graduating class events, and BIPOC for Black, Indigenous, People of Colour student experiences and awareness.

records.title: Swimming & Lifesaving Program
facts: The Swimming Program is offered during the winter term.
It includes an optional Lifesaving component.
Lifesaving courses are provided by the Cowichan Aquatic Centre and facilitated by the swimming coach.
Students learn water rescue education, aquatic facility supervision, and lifeguarding skills.
The program welcomes all students, including those who cannot swim at the start.
Coaches group swimmers based on their ability level at the start of the term.
Non-swimmers receive support to pass the Swim to Survive test.
Sue Whitney is a coach for Swimming & Lifesaving.

records.title: Technology Orientation
facts: During orientation, the Innovations Team conducts a short seminar to cover initial technology setup for students.

records.title: Tennis Program
keywords: BC Independent Schools Association Championship Tournament
facts: The Tennis Program is available year-round as a sports choice.
The school has eight outdoor tennis courts on campus for practice and competitions.
Students can also use Arbutus Ridge Golf Club's tennis bubble, an all-weather facility with three courts, during colder months.
The program is open to students of all levels as a recreational sport.
It offers both junior and senior competitive programs.
The program focuses on skill development leading up to the competitive season in the spring.
Extra practice time is available during spare afternoons and on weekends on the on-campus courts.

Competition opportunities include the Vancouver Island Regional Championship Tournament, BC Independent Schools Association Championship Tournament (Islands), and BC Secondary Provincial Championships (Provincials).
The team won Gold Medals at the 2024 Islands and achieved 4th place at Provincials.
Conrad Alscher and Tiara Hobbs are coaches for the Tennis program.

records.title: Theatre Production Program
facts: Students can join the Theatre Production Program to support performing arts from behind the scenes.
Creative opportunities include stage management, lighting-console operation, sound editing and design, projections, special effects, and theatrical design.
Students learn to set up and operate sound and lighting equipment.
They run technical aspects for in-house productions such as the annual musical, evening concerts, dance showcase, and weekly assemblies.
The instructor is Hilary Britton-Foster.

records.title: Tripartite Program
facts: Brentwood developed a unique Tripartite Program.
The program integrates academics, athletics, and arts.

records.title: University Preparatory Program
facts: Brentwood College School provides a University Preparatory Program with support for planning university studies in Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and other countries.
The university counselling process begins formally at the end of Grade 10 with guidance on course selection for Grade 11.
In Grades 11 and 12, individual Advisors and the University Counselling Team assist students in understanding their options.
Parents are encouraged to participate in developing potential post-secondary choices.
Opportunities to visit university campuses are typically available during the fall midterm break in early November.

records.title: Unrivalled Opportunities
facts: Brentwood offers unrivalled opportunities in academics, arts, and athletics.
A timetable is available for viewing these opportunities.

records.title: Volleyball Program
facts: The Brentwood Volleyball Program offers three junior girls teams (Grades 8-10) and two senior girls teams (Grades 11-12).
Teams vary in skill level, accommodating both new and experienced players.
During the fall term, competitive Junior and Senior Girls teams compete against top provincial teams.
In 2023, the senior team won the Island Championship and placed 5th at BC's AAA Provincials.
The winter term focuses on skill development, and players can participate in local club programs.
The coaching staff consists of former national, university, and high school volleyball players.

records.title: Waterfront Activities
facts: The rowing program has produced 24 Olympic rowers and hosted regattas for over 50 years. Outdoor pursuits students kayak and canoe in Saanich Inlet, with overnight trips to Gulf Islands. Docks allow swimming in warm weather.

records.title: Woodworking Program
facts: Students learn to use machine and hand tools to construct functional and artistic projects.
The program teaches skills such as cutting, creating wood joints, sanding, and applying stains, waxes, and other finishes.
Advanced opportunities allow students to design their own projects.
Safety is a priority, with students trained on equipment in a graduated manner and supervised by instructors.

records.title: Yoga Mental Grit Program
facts: Yoga Mental Grit is a structured program designed to build resilience through disciplined habits, deliberate discomfort, and nervous system regulation.
The program aims to develop mental fortitude, self-mastery, and self-leadership.
Students enhance mental grit by practicing repetitive movement sequences, breath control, cold-immersion training, and recovery practices.
Most classes are held outdoors on Tuesdays and Thursdays, with Saturdays dedicated to relaxation.
This program is for students willing to build disciplined habits, embrace challenge, strengthen focus, and seek self-mastery.

records.title: Youth Spring Break Camps
facts: Brentwood College School offers youth spring break camps on its campus, located on one kilometer of shoreline in Mill Bay.
The campus provides an ideal environment for learning new skills and making friends.
Enrolment is open when a 'register now' button is visible for individual camp offerings.
Further details and documentation are provided by each program director upon registration and payment.
Questions can be directed to the Facility Rentals Team at events@brentwood.ca.

records.title: 2026 Strategic Plan - Grit & Joy
facts: Brentwood's 2026 Strategic Plan, titled "Grit & Joy," guides the school's future, building on values introduced in 2013.
The plan's purpose is "Preparing Students For Life."
It outlines four enduring commitments: Learning, Boarding, Team, and Family.
The plan emphasizes a balanced and rigorous education through the Tripartite Program (academics, athletics, arts), aiming to inspire and support each student.
It focuses on a vibrant and immersive campus experience, fostering relationships and skills, and ensuring belonging and respect for differences within the boarding model.
The plan also commits to retaining and attracting talented staff and strengthening operational sustainability.
It aims to foster a connected community, locally and internationally, by engaging alumni, parents, and partners, and by teaching social responsibility and global perspectives.
Garth Chalmers is the Head of School, and Karen (Middleton) Pirie is the Chair of the Board.

Evening Prep is supervised academic study from 7:30 pm to 9:30 pm on weeknights in the houses.

records.title: Brentwood College School Overview
facts: Brentwood College School is a university preparatory private school located in Mill Bay, British Columbia, Canada.
The school hosts an international community with students from over 50 countries annually.

records.title: Brentwood College School Timetable
facts: Brentwood's Tripartite Program integrates academics, arts, and athletics.
Academic classes run mornings, Monday-Saturday, with three alternating blocks daily.
Arts are Monday, Wednesday, Friday afternoons, offering up to four hour-long courses.
Athletics are Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday afternoons, with students choosing a different sport each term.
The timetable includes a 'Cookie Break' and tutorial blocks on Tuesday and Friday mornings.

records.title: Brentwood Family Community
facts: The Brentwood Family encompasses current students, parents, alumni, past parents, and staff.
It serves as a connected community for friends, colleagues, mentors, and mentees.

records.title: Brentwood's Core Philosophy
facts: Brentwood College empowers students to discover their passions through choices and opportunities.
It builds strong relationships within its engaged, authentic, and inclusive global community through the boarding school environment.
The school's philosophy includes grit, joy, humility, engagement, balance, and authenticity.

records.title: Campus and Educational Approach
facts: The school features an oceanfront campus.
Its modern education is guided by a unique timetable designed to provide opportunities in academics, athletics, and arts.

records.title: Directions to Brentwood College School

The M.V. Coho travels from Port Angeles, WA, and FRS Clipper from Seattle, WA.

records.title: School History
facts: Brentwood College School was founded in 1923 in Brentwood Bay, Vancouver Island.
The original campus was destroyed by fire in 1947.
The school was re-established in September 1961 on the shores of Mill Bay.
In 1972, Brentwood became the first all-boys boarding school in Canada to become co-educational.

records.title: School Life & Facilities
facts: Academic facilities include technology-equipped classrooms and outdoor teaching spaces.
School life features weekly assemblies, a Wednesday "Sleep-in," and Saturday night events like arts, athletics, and house open houses.
Food services provide healthy meals, snacks, and Sunday brunch.

records.title: School Philosophy and Values
facts: Brentwood College School, established in 1923, focuses on creating the best learning experience for students.

Core values include Grit (hard work, perseverance), Joy (inclusive community, optimism), Humility (teamwork, service), Engagement (deep relationships), Balance (measured approach, rest), and Authenticity (diverse, inclusive culture).

records.title: School Philosophy and Values
facts: Brentwood College School was established in 1923.
The school's culture is guided by core values: Grit, Joy, Humility, Engagement, Balance, and Authenticity.
Grit involves hard work, perseverance, and accountability.
Joy emphasizes a close-knit, inclusive community that encourages excellence and new experiences.
Humility values everyone's place and purpose, promoting teamwork and service.
Engagement encourages full participation in school life to build lasting relationships.
Balance provides a stable platform for success, recognizing mistakes as part of learning and promoting a well-rounded attitude.
Authenticity prioritizes diverse, inclusive, and equitable experiences, welcoming students and staff from all backgrounds.

records.title: School Purpose and Values
facts: Brentwood's core purpose is "Preparing Students For Life."
The school's driving values are Grit and Joy, which are explored and celebrated daily by students and staff.
These values are considered fundamental to success and align with the school's purpose.

records.title: Social Responsibility and Community Engagement
facts: Brentwood's philosophy emphasizes inclusion, respect, and accountability to its environment and the wider world.
The school positively impacts the local community through service, partnerships, and bursaries.
Student volunteer programs like B-Well and BEAT engage in community service.
The annual Brentwood Service Day involves over 500 volunteers aiding local families and fundraising for Cowichan Valley non-profits.
B-Well supports organizations such as the Canadian Cancer Society, C.M.S.
Food Bank, and Warmland House.
Annual fundraising supports Student Financial Aid, increasing access to education.

records.title: Strategic Commitments
facts: The school has four key commitments for its ongoing development: Learning, Boarding, Team, and Family.
"Learning" focuses on balanced and rigorous education through the Tripartite Program, promoting discovery, challenge, and wellbeing, and supporting students in and out of the classroom.
"Boarding" aims for a vibrant campus experience, embedding a curriculum for relationships and skills, and ensuring belonging and respect for differences.
"Team" involves attracting and retaining talented staff who embody the school's culture and adopting practices for operational sustainability.
"Family" emphasizes a connected community, locally and internationally, enriching learning through alumni, parent, and partner engagement, and modeling social responsibility and global perspectives.

records.title: Student Culture and Community

Students from around the world share cuisine, history, and customs, enriching the experience.
This helps students learn communication, humility, and respect.

records.title: Wellness Framework
facts: The Brentwood Wellness Framework is a proactive tool to support student reflection, personal development, and identify available supports.
It aims to empower students to take ownership of their wellness and develop a stronger sense of well-being.
Wellness promotion is integrated into all aspects of the school program.
Students can develop skills and strategies to navigate stressors and build resilience.
For more intense challenges, students can access targeted skills and strategies through the school.
Temporary needs-based flexibility in academics, arts, or athletics may be provided with the goal of returning to full capacity.
In crisis situations preventing safe articulation on campus, students will be taken into the care of their parent(s) or guardian(s).
